503811|2026-03.headline: Siyaram Q4 FY26 total income rose 16.1% YoY to INR 871 crores, PAT up 30.6% to INR 95 crores; FY27 revenue growth guided at about 12%.
503811|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 standalone total income was INR 871 crores (up 16.1% YoY) with EBITDA of INR 152 crores (17.4% margin, up 21%) and PAT of INR 95 crores (up 30.6%). Full-year FY26 total income reached INR 2,653 crores (up 15.5%), EBITDA INR 413 crores (15.6% margin) and PAT INR 228 crores (up 14.8%). Management said demand improved gradually in Q4 on wedding and festive season, while input-cost volatility and geopolitics remain a concern. The company announced a special interim dividend of INR 4 and final dividend of INR 5 per share (INR 16 total for FY26), plus a small residential project at Dombivali. Store count reached 44 (27 ZECODE, 17 DEVO), with a target of about 70 by FY27 end.

financial_highlights.value: INR 16 per share (special interim INR 4 + final INR 5 plus other components per management)

segments.name: Fabric
segments.commentary: About 80% of FY26 revenue. Volume grew about 10% and value about 11%, with management attributing growth mainly to market share gains and a favourable wedding season.

segments.name: Garments (ex-retail)
segments.commentary: About 15% of FY26 revenue. Volume grew about 9% and value about 8%, excluding the new retail business.

segments.name: Retail (ZECODE and DEVO)
segments.commentary: Company-owned stores, 44 at quarter end (27 ZECODE, 17 DEVO). FY26 retail revenue about INR 80 crores, with EBITDA drag within the guided 150 bps. Target of about 70 stores by FY27 end.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: About 10% of revenue in FY26, stable at 9-10% over recent years. Management did not give a share target.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at about 12%.
EBITDA margin guided at about 14%, with about 150 bps drag from retail; management cautioned this is subject to volatile input prices.
Store count to reach about 70 (ZECODE and DEVO) by end of FY27, implying about 26 additions, of which about 8 DEVO and the rest ZECODE; all company-owned (COCO), no franchising this year.
FY27 capex about INR 100 crores: INR 50-60 crores maintenance plus about INR 40 crores for new stores.
Ad spend guided at 4-5% of revenue.

Residential project at Dombivali (about 77,000 sq ft) to start June 2026, about 24 months; total outlay about INR 45-60 crores (incl. land per one reply), revenue about INR 80 crores; about INR 25 crores spend in FY27.

Preferential issue of RPS: NCLT final hearing done 16 April; order expected first week of June 2026, with about 3-4 months more to issue RPS. Management said RPS issue will not affect cash flows this year.
New ZECODE geographies planned in FY27: Bangalore radius, Chennai/Tamil Nadu, Hyderabad, south Maharashtra.
capex_capacity: FY27 capex about INR 100 crores: INR 50-60 crores regular maintenance plus about INR 40 crores for about 26 new stores.
Inventory per new company-owned store about INR 60-70 lakh.
Inventory days about 135-138 at March, similar to last year per management.
Dombivali residential project about 77,000 sq ft built-up, construction from June 2026, 24-month timeline; not treated as capex but as cash outflow.
Store sizes shifting to 6,000-10,000 sq ft (average about 7,000-8,000 sq ft) from earlier 4,000-5,000 sq ft.
demand_pricing: Management said consumer demand improved gradually in Q4, helped by income tax relief, wedding and festive season.
Raw material prices volatile; pass-through to consumers is gradual to protect volumes and market share.
Management expects branded players to gain share as input prices rise and the branded-unbranded gap narrows; said this is a longer-term play.
Legacy fabric business expected to grow high single digit to low double digit in FY27.
Q1 flagged as seasonally weakest quarter; management also cited geopolitics, raw material issues and heat wave.

qa_highlights.question: FY27 capex and store guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR 100 crores capex: INR 50-60 crores maintenance plus about INR 40 crores for stores, taking the count to about 70 by year end.

qa_highlights.question: Will EBITDA margin guidance be raised?
qa_highlights.answer: No change; management retained about 14% EBITDA margin guidance with 150 bps retail drag, subject to input price volatility.

qa_highlights.question: Retail FY26 revenue and margin drag?
qa_highlights.answer: Retail revenue about INR 80 crores versus INR 70-80 crores estimate; EBITDA drag was within the 150 bps budget. FY27 drag again guided at about 1.5%.

qa_highlights.question: Why were FY26 store openings short of guidance (35 planned)?
qa_highlights.answer: Lean start-up team focused on operations; some sites were under-construction properties, delaying openings. FY27 target set more conservatively at about 70 total stores.

qa_highlights.question: Growth split between market share and channel inventory?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth was largely market share gain, with favourable wedding season; fabric market grows only a small percentage.

qa_highlights.question: Why did inventory and debtors rise about 25%?
qa_highlights.answer: Partly new stores (inventory held on books), partly build-up ahead of a strong Q4; inventory days stable at about 135-138. Operating cash flow about INR 150 crores, with large part absorbed by inventory and debtors.

qa_highlights.question: Other income composition for FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Interest about INR 27 crores, profit on sale of assets about INR 21 crores, MTM gain about INR 12.73 crores, capital subsidy INR 5.31 crores. Remaining government grants about INR 5-6 crores pending.

qa_highlights.question: Residential project economics and revenue recognition?
qa_highlights.answer: Outlay about INR 45 crores over the 24-month project on owned land, revenue about INR 80 crores; revenue to be recognised on completion certificate as per standard.

risks_watch: Input cost volatility (cotton and other raw materials) and gradual pass-through could pressure the 14% EBITDA margin guidance.
Retail store economics still immature; most stores under one year old, and management withheld per-store revenue and EBITDA break-even data.
Store additions slowed: FY26 achieved about 26 against 35 guided; FY27 target of about 70 total depends on finding sites.
Working capital: inventory and debtors up about 25%; net cash flow from operations of about INR 93 crores versus PAT of INR 228 crores drew questions.
Preferential RPS issue timing depends on NCLT order (expected first week of June 2026), then about 3-4 months to issue shares.
Dombivali real estate project is outside core business; revenue recognition on completion and actual sellable area not yet confirmed.

503811|2026-06.headline: Siyaram Silk Q1 FY27 total income rose 16.4% to INR466 crores, EBITDA up 22.3% to INR40 crores at 8.6% margin, PAT INR11 crores.
503811|2026-06.overview: Standalone total income grew 16.4% YoY to INR466 crores, with fabrics at 71% of revenue, garments 19% and yarn & others 10%. EBITDA rose 22.3% to INR40 crores, margin 8.6%, and PAT more than doubled to INR11 crores (PAT margin 2.4%) on operating leverage. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of ~12% revenue growth and ~14% EBITDA margin including retail, with a ~150 bps EBITDA drag from ZECODE and DEVO. Adhik Maas moderated wedding demand in the quarter, and Diwali is expected to be ~3 weeks later this year.

FY27 expectation ~INR160 crores vs ~INR70-80 crores in FY26

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance (including retail): ~12% revenue growth and ~14% EBITDA margin, reiterated by management.
Retail drag on annual EBITDA margin guided at ~150 bps; management said it expects to be well within that budget. Stated as a ballpark, including all store costs (rent included per management).
ZECODE store profitability expected in 1.5 to 2 years; some ZECODE stores already EBITDA positive, including some under one year old.
FY27 capex about INR100 crores, of which INR40-50 crores for retail; management expects positive free cash flow to remain this year.
Store expansion to accelerate only after business predictability and proof of mature store model; ~70 stores targeted in FY27, funded by internal accruals.
Real estate project (land development): construction expected to start in Q1 FY27, 24-month completion; no revenue booked yet.

Average ZECODE store size moved from ~4,000 sq ft high-street formats to ~7,000 sq ft, which management says performs better.
FY27 capex ~INR100 crores, with INR40-50 crores for retail; management said spend is not a concern given positive surplus cash flow.
Real estate: INR24.6 crores of land development cost passed through P&L with an equal reversal from inventory (net nil); 24-month construction timeline.
Franchise model considered an option later but not pursued; company is using internal capital for stores.
demand_pricing: Demand stable in Q1 but wedding and occasion-led purchases moderated during Adhik Maas; consumers value-conscious and input-cost inflation persisted.
Diwali pushed back about 3 weeks this year, which management expects to delay demand; management said sentiment for the season is positive.
Some price pass-on taken in Q1, and further pass-on planned gradually if raw material costs stay high; management said raw material inflation is volatile and cannot be fully passed through.
ZECODE targets Gen Z in Karnataka/Bangalore first; fast fashion described as a large, faster-growing market with many competitors.
Asset-light, rotating inventory model lets the company shift quickly between categories; working capital build is seasonal ahead of festive and wedding seasons.

qa_highlights.question: How are ZECODE store profitability and breakeven tracking amid competition?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said stores are ~18 months old and profitability is targeted in 1.5-2 years; some stores are EBITDA positive, including some under a year old, but it is too early to conclude.

qa_highlights.question: How much EBITDA loss does retail carry and is the 150 bps drop inclusive of rent?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the ~150 bps annual EBITDA drop is a ballpark that includes all store operating costs and rent; it is not measured quarterly and the company will not disclose separate ZECODE/DEVO numbers yet.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the Q1 margin improvement, excluding the INR24-25 crore land development cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the land cost was moved from inventory to expenses, so the net effect is nil and EBITDA margins are unchanged; the quarter should not be modelled alone given seasonality.

qa_highlights.question: What is the retail revenue outlook and what would trigger faster store expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Retail revenue was ~INR30 crores in Q1 with FY27 at ~INR160 crores; management will accelerate expansion only after store maturity and scale in infrastructure and technology.

qa_highlights.question: How is raw material inflation expected to affect margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said some pass-on was taken in Q1 with more possible if margins compress, and it reiterated the ~14% EBITDA margin guidance including the retail drag.

qa_highlights.question: Is other income one-off?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said other income is mostly recurring (delayed payment interest, rent); management said about 30% is a mark-to-market gain that varies quarter to quarter.

risks_watch: Retail EBITDA drag (~150 bps) depends on store maturity; ZECODE profitability not yet proven and DEVO performance untested beyond the festive season.
Working capital: inventory and receivables built in March; management says March-to-March comparison is the right gauge and extra inventory will rise with store count.
Raw material and chemical cost volatility, with pass-through to customers only partial.
Diwali delayed about 3 weeks, which could shift festive revenue between Q2 and Q3.

Preference share bonus issue: record date 22 August 2026; tax treatment for investors not settled and listing/sale treatment still to be confirmed.

503811|2026-09.headline: Siyaram Q2 FY27 total income rose 15.1% to Rs 827 crore, but PAT fell to Rs 75 crore from Rs 87 crore; revenue guidance raised to 14-15%.
503811|2026-09.overview: Standalone total income grew 15.1% YoY to Rs 827 crore in Q2 FY27, and H1 total income rose 15.6% to Rs 1,293 crore. EBITDA rose to Rs 131 crore from Rs 121 crore, but PAT declined to Rs 75 crore from Rs 87 crore, with raw material inflation cited as the main margin drag. Management raised FY27 revenue growth guidance to 14-15% and kept the ~14% EBITDA guidance (before a 150 bps retail-driven drop). Retail (ZECODE and DEVO) scaled to 61 stores against a 70-store year-end target.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said volume rose roughly 2.5% and value roughly 11%, while preferring absolute values over the volume-value split due to mix changes.

qa_highlights.question: Price hikes and gross margin decline?
qa_highlights.answer: Cumulative price hikes of about 4%-6% over six months; gross margin decline mainly from raw material inflation, with retail a smaller factor.

qa_highlights.answer: H1 retail revenue about Rs 65 crore (ZECODE + DEVO); FY27 target about Rs 160 crore; store count target 70 at FY27 end, with no 75-80 guidance given.

504028|2026-03.headline: GEE Q4 FY26 turnover rose to INR112 crore and FY26 to about INR370 crore, with EBITDA margin near 9% and a 25-30% revenue CAGR target to FY29.
504028|2026-03.overview: Management described Q4 FY26 turnover of about INR112 crore (up from INR79 crore in Q1 FY26), taking FY26 to roughly INR370 crore versus INR334 crore in FY25. Q4 EBITDA was about INR33 crore at a 9% margin, and PAT about INR13 crore (3.5% margin). Management framed FY26 as a stabilisation year after the May 2025 promoter restructuring, and set targets of INR1,000 crore revenue by FY29-30, FY27 revenue above INR500 crore and EBITDA margin above 10%. Growth is tied to defence, power (nuclear, thermal, hydro), railways and exports, with flux-cored wire production slated to start in July 2026.

financial_highlights.change: up from INR79 crore in Q1 FY26 (sequential)
management says FY25 margins were stabilised and exceeded in the last couple of years

financial_highlights.value: under 10% of revenue; around INR350-plus crore of INR370 crore is domestic
financial_highlights.change: down from a higher share in earlier years

segments.name: Specialised/defence products
segments.commentary: Management says GEE holds 70-80% share in defence welding consumables (Griduct 100, GEEFLUX 521); specialised applications business was about INR25 crore per an analyst's figure, which management did not confirm. FY26 defence business was INR10-12 crore, planned to more than double in FY27.

segments.name: Flux-cored wires
segments.commentary: Import-driven business of INR25-30 crore a year; in-house production expected from July 2026 under new BIS rules, with management targeting more than INR50 crore revenue a year and adding lines over time. Management set a North Star of INR 1,000 crores revenue by FY29-30, with 10-13% EBITDA margin ambitions, supported by a NPCIL approval, new SAW wire, SAW flux and flux cored wire lines, and a Thane land monetisation. 504028|2026-09.headline: GEE Ltd H1 FY27 turnover rose 24% to INR 204 crore, but Q2 margins compressed on input-cost inflation; management targets 25-30% growth and 12-13% EBITDA margin.
504028|2026-09.overview: Management reported H1 FY27 turnover of about INR 204 crore (up 24% from INR 165 crore), EBITDA of about INR 16 crore (up 17.5% from INR 13.5 crore) and PBT of about INR 10.7 crore (from about INR 7 crore). Management attributed margin pressure in the quarter to steel and oil price spikes linked to the Middle East war, and said gross margins should recover. The Wagle Industrial Estate land was handed to a developer for a real estate project, with management guiding to INR 400 crore-plus of revenue to the company over five years. The call also set out capacity expansion, new product verticals and a INR 1,000 crore revenue target by FY30.

segments.commentary: Consolidated capacity about 59,000 MT (Kolkata plant 38,000 MT; second facility 21,000 MT). Specialised/niche products are about 27% of the basket, targeted at 35-40% in the coming year; conventional products sell at about INR 100-125/kg versus INR 275-1,500/kg for specialised products.

segments.name: Real estate (Wagle Industrial Estate, Thane)
segments.commentary: Land possession handed to developer under area-share revenue model; company expects INR 400 crore-plus revenue over five years, with sales and cash accruals starting from the first quarter of next financial year.

guidance_outlook: Top-line growth target of 25-30% YoY, with roughly 60% from volume and 40% from value per management's split.
Sustainable EBITDA margin of 12-13% targeted in three to four years; management cited 0.5% gain in FY27, a further 0.5-1% in FY28, and double-digit margin in FY28.
Q3 and Q4 FY27 EBITDA margin expected to be restored to 9% and above.
INR 1,000 crore revenue target placed realistically at FY30; capacity to rise from 59,000 MT to 71,000 MT with over 90% utilisation by FY29-FY30.
Export turnover target of 15-20% of total in the next two to three years.
Working capital to fall below 100 days by year-end, and to market peer levels by FY28.
Real estate proceeds to fund brownfield acquisitions (tier-two/three welding companies) and shareholder rewards, with no debt-funded acquisitions.
Capex of INR 30-40 crore over two years for new product lines, with expected 18-20% returns.
capex_capacity: Capex outlay of INR 35-40 crore over next two years (analyst-cited range of INR 30-40 crore), for two new product verticals and capacity expansion.

SOFT FLUX lines also planned as a new vertical.
MIG wires (continuous wires and wire rods): about 12,000 MT capacity, 100% utilised; plan to add another 12,000 MT to reach 24,000 MT.

demand_pricing: Management says the company is at about 6-6.5% share of the organised market, targeting 10-12% at INR 1,000 crore revenue; the organised segment is cited at about 55% of a INR 12,000 crore market.
More than 130 new dealers added in the last six months; more than 500 dealers across India, exports to about 20 countries.
Price pass-through: input price increases pass on with a 15-25 day lag; price cuts are passed on with a similar lag.
Sales split of about 55:45 between direct B2B/B2C and dealers/distributors, per management.

Gross margin pressure attributed to temporary input-cost spikes (steel, oil) linked to the Middle East war, not product mix.
Historically about 55%+ of revenue in H2 and 40-45% in H1, due to monsoon seasonality.
Other expenses rose to INR 12.5 crore, attributed to approval and market-penetration costs.

qa_highlights.question: When will the company receive cash from the real estate project and in what form?
qa_highlights.answer: Cash accruals start from Q1 of next financial year as sales begin at launch; no developer advance, as it is an area-share model with the company selling its own share, with a mix of outright sale, long-term lease and retained units.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margin decline, and what is the margin guidance?

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses rise from INR 9.5 crore to INR 12.5 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there was no specific one-off; the increase reflects costs of securing approvals and market penetration.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the rise in inventory days and borrowings?

qa_highlights.question: How does the company plan to reach 12-13% EBITDA margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Through product mix (specialised share from 27% to 35-40%), price premium from approvals and brand, and economies of scale from higher capacity utilisation.

504036|2026-06.headline: Hirect Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 20.3% to INR258.4 crore, but EBITDA fell 45.4% YoY to INR13.2 crore as Elventive France drags margins.

Standalone revenue grew 10.1% to INR236.4 crore and standalone EBITDA rose 3.2% to INR25.1 crore at a 10.6% margin. Management expects Elventive France margin drag to persist for another 3 to 5 quarters before breakeven.

504036|2026-09.headline: Hirect Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 39% YoY to INR315.7 crore, but consolidated EBITDA margin fell to 4.3% on Elventive France and margin pressure.

504132|2026-09.headline: Q2 FY27 standalone revenue rose 49% YoY to INR72.5 crore and EBITDA rose 159% to INR17.8 crore, led by EV demand.
504132|2026-09.overview: Standalone revenue from operations was INR72.5 crore in Q2 FY27, up 49% YoY, driven by higher EV-application supplies, mainly to export customers. EBITDA was INR17.8 crore (25% margin) versus 14% a year earlier and 19% in Q1, attributed to product mix and operating leverage. Alloys revenue grew in H1 but a new furnace ran below capacity due to teething issues, so FY27 alloys guidance was cut to INR40-50 crore. Relays commercial ramp-up slipped to FY28, and Quantum Magnetics product approvals have not started, so FY27 revenue from that segment is now expected to be nil.

segments.name: Automotive / EV
segments.commentary: Q2 FY27 automotive sales were INR24 crore, up from INR15 crore in Q1 and INR10.5 crore in Q2 FY26. Management says the uptick came from existing customer programs (mostly export, two to three customers), with similar levels expected for the rest of FY27.

segments.commentary: Demand picked up modestly in H1 FY27 from a few select customers, and management expects similar levels going forward, dependent on utility installation pace. A water meter product is in pilot stage, with about 2,000-3,000 parts supplied; management sizes it at INR5-10 crore per product for one customer.

segments.name: Alloys
segments.commentary: H1 FY27 revenue was about INR12 crore because the new furnace had breakdowns. FY27 is now guided at INR40-50 crore, versus an earlier 3-4x FY26 expectation (about INR70-80 crore). Virgin-alloy gross margin is 10-15%, and returns-based 15-25%; FY27 EBITDA margin is about breakeven or slightly higher.

segments.name: Relays
segments.commentary: Pilot supplies are expected in H2 FY27, but commercial ramp-up has moved to FY28 after customer testing iterations. Management expects 15-20% gross margin, with no customer offtake agreements signed yet.

segments.name: Quantum Magnetics
segments.commentary: Phase 2 (block cutting, machining, surface treatment) was commissioned in October 2026. Management now expects no FY27 revenue, versus an earlier INR5-10 crore guide. FY28 could be INR10-40 crore depending on one customer's share. ECMS approval gives 25% of capex as incentive, subject to conditions.

Management cited Chinese EV dominance and possible restrictions in Western markets as a factor for Western EV demand, but said it has no concrete data.

qa_highlights.question: What changed in EV demand, and will it sustain into FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Demand rose from existing export customer programs, partly deferred earlier and now recovering. Customers indicate similar levels for H2 FY27, but there is no FY28 forecast; management expects similar levels.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins stay at 20%+ if EV demand holds?
qa_highlights.answer: Margin depends on product mix; export margins are higher. If EV demand stays at Q2 levels, margins should be similar to Q2, though management did not commit to a specific number.

qa_highlights.question: Has the FY27 alloys target changed, and what margins apply?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 alloys revenue is now INR40-50 crore (H1 about INR12 crore), down from earlier expectations because of lost months from teething issues. Virgin-alloy gross margin is 10-15%, returns 15-25%; FY28 could be INR70-80 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Quantum Magnetics INR5-10 crore FY27 revenue guidance still on track?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management expects no FY27 revenue because the customer needs visits, plant audits and product approval first; FY28 is 'INR10-40 crore' depending on customer share.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the INR400 crore PLI/MeitY capex and equipment pricing?

risks_watch: EV demand concentration: two to three export customers, with no FY28 orders or forecast. Management noted the risk of Chinese EV competition and entry barriers in the West.
Alloys execution: furnace breakdowns, supplier issues, and customer delay penalties; H2 FY27 utilisation must improve to reach INR40-50 crore.
Relays and Quantum Magnetics: both depend on customer approvals with no offtake agreements. Quantum also depends on imported blocks, with China export restrictions a risk.
Management said it may not be able to give a clear FY28 growth number until about three months from the call.

504341|2026-09.headline: Ravindra Energy H1 FY27 consolidated PAT fell to INR 20.7 crore from INR 46.6 crore as Energy in Motion losses widened; Q2 EIM sales rose to 142 vehicles.
504341|2026-09.overview: Management reported Q2 FY27 total revenue of INR 190 crore and H1 revenue of INR 310 crore (vs INR 287 crore), with renewable EBITDA up to INR 53 crore in Q2 from INR 33.4 crore. Consolidated PAT after Energy in Motion (EIM) losses was INR 19 crore in Q2 (vs INR 24.4 crore) and INR 20.7 crore in H1 (vs INR 46.6 crore). EIM sold 142 electric trucks in Q2 vs 58 in Q1 and says the second half will be significantly stronger, with losses expected to narrow in Q3 and Q4. Operating renewable capacity is 261.21 MW with 231.10 MW under construction, targeting 500 MW by March 2027.

segments.commentary: Network sales INR 10.7 crore in Q2 vs INR 6.5 crore in Q1. Eight charging stations today, targeted at 15 by December 2026 and 40 by March 2027. Swaps per station utilisation below 30%.

504380|2026-06.headline: Flomic Q1 FY27 revenue rose 18.4% YoY to INR120 crore and EBITDA margin expanded 275 bps to 9.34%, but PAT fell to INR2.06 crore from INR2.98 crore.
504380|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations grew 18.4% YoY to INR120 crore, with management attributing most of the growth to higher freight rates rather than volume (shipments up roughly 6-7%). EBITDA rose about 68% to INR11.21 crore and margin improved to 9.34% from 6.59%. PBT turned positive at INR2.73 crore from a loss of INR3.3 crore a year earlier, while PAT was INR2.06 crore versus INR2.98 crore last year. Management said a one-time INR28 lakh lease-related benefit was included, and it cited branch closures, manpower cost reduction and an AI-based back-office system from 1 July as margin levers.

segments.name: Air & Sea Import Forwarding
segments.commentary: Revenue INR40 crore in Q1; management said all segments improved YoY, but no prior-year split was given.

segments.name: Sea Export
segments.commentary: Revenue around INR33.39 crore in Q1; management said ocean exports are the main incremental profit pool while freight rates are rising.

segments.name: Air Export
segments.commentary: Revenue INR22 crore in Q1; management said some cargo has shifted from ocean to air, adding to this segment.

segments.name: Warehousing
segments.commentary: Revenue INR18 crore in Q1; around 15% of revenue now, with a stated gross margin of 15-16% (15-20% range), targeted at 17-18% and then about 20% of contribution.

segments.name: Air & Sea Import Clearance
segments.commentary: Revenue INR7.42 crore in Q1; management did not give further detail.

guidance_outlook: Management expects revenue growth momentum to continue for three to four quarters, but gave no numerical FY27 target.
Management expects ocean and air export benefits to last at least two to three more quarters while freight rates stay elevated.
Management said freight rate-driven growth may not be long-term sustainable.
Warehousing share of revenue is targeted to rise to 17-18% and then about 20%.
Management expects operating margins to improve further from corrective actions, higher freight rates and AI-led cost reduction.
Management says it will stay asset-light, with warehousing expansion mainly leased and customer-backed.
capex_capacity: Warehousing expansion will be selective, leased and customer-backed rather than driven by square footage.
Project cargo vertical is being built with a newly hired team; management called it higher margin but higher execution risk.
AI-based application (back-office documentation, quotation-to-billing) started from 1 July 2026; the company handled about 42,000 shipments last year, previously with manual file creation.
Priorities for FY27 include CFS and air cargo capabilities, presence across key Indian hubs and selectively overseas.
No capex amount or capacity figures were disclosed.
demand_pricing: Revenue growth was mainly price-driven: shipment volumes rose about 6-7% YoY, with the rest from freight rates, which rose sharply on geopolitical volatility.
Middle East disruption reduced export cargo volumes, per management.
Management targets mid-sized customers and avoids both very large corporates and small startups, citing margin and payment risk.
Project cargo demand cited from oil and gas, aerospace, energy, pharma cold chain and solar; exports mainly to Africa, imports from Germany and China.
Management did not disclose the customer count beyond an analyst's reference to about 5,000 active customers.

qa_highlights.question: How does management view FY27 revenue growth for Flomic?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects revenue to be better on higher freight rates, with momentum for three to four quarters, but gave no number.

qa_highlights.question: What is the scale and margin profile of the project logistics business?
qa_highlights.answer: Management described oversized, dimensional project cargo needing special equipment and permits, with higher margins than routine freight forwarding and higher execution risk; no revenue scale was given.

qa_highlights.question: How much of Q1 revenue growth came from volume versus price?
qa_highlights.answer: Shipment growth was about 6-7% YoY; the remainder came from freight rate increases.

qa_highlights.question: What is the sustainable margin after excluding the one-time INR28 lakh benefit?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said PAT margin was still significantly higher YoY even after excluding the INR28 lakh, and that manpower cost has already been reduced.

qa_highlights.question: What is the warehousing margin and growth potential?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said warehousing gross margin is 15-16% (15-20% range), with Ind AS 116 inflating reported segment margin because rent on leased assets is excluded; share of revenue is to rise to about 20%.

qa_highlights.answer: No savings figure was given; management said closed branches were non-performing and located where the company lacked customers.

Management attributed most of the growth to sharply higher freight rates on India-US and Latin American lanes, with volumes up about 6-7% in Q1. Warehousing expansion at Bhiwandi (vertical multi-tier and pallet racking) was completed in Q2 with customers already occupying the new space.

guidance_outlook: Warehousing share of revenue to rise from about 13-14% to 17-18% over the coming quarters and about 20% within three to five years, driven by customer-backed expansion.

Warehousing expansion expected to add about INR1 crore annual revenue if the two Bhiwandi additions run at 100% capacity; the 15,000 sq ft storage adds about INR50 lakh a year and the 2,000+ pallet positions about INR40-50 lakh once occupied.
H2 FY27 priorities: scale warehousing to customer demand, strengthen project cargo and specialized logistics, deepen integrated services with existing customers, and use technology for efficiency.
Management said freight rate elevation is not uniform across routes and that margin, not rate movement, is the focus; no formal numerical guidance was given.
capex_capacity: Bhiwandi multi-tier storage (ground plus three tiers) commissioned July 2026 and completed September 2026; adds 15,000 sq ft, lifting leasable area of the same footprint from 5,000 to 20,000 sq ft; purchased outright, not leased. Quick commerce customer occupying since September.

Network: 25 branches and more than 30 warehouses across India; new sales offices being considered based on manufacturing and import-export potential.
demand_pricing: Freight rates on India to US 40-foot containers rose from about $2,800 (end February/March) to about $9,600 (August/September), per management; rates doubled to tripled.
Growth in Q2 was described as largely driven by freight rate increases rather than volume; Q1 volume growth was about 6-7%.
Gross margin percentage is roughly constant on freight, so higher turnover lowers GP margin percentage while lifting absolute profit.
Repeat customers were 51% of FY26 business; top 15 customers were more than 20% of turnover. Over 5,000 active customers; more than 42,000 shipments in FY26.
Air freight: contractual space agreements with several carriers; export focus on US, South America and Africa.
Geopolitical disruption (Gulf) has lengthened lead and transit times, but cargo is still moving via alternate routings.

qa_highlights.question: Plans to expand the domestic branch network and location selection criteria?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is open to opening new sales offices where potential exists; selection is based on manufacturing base and import-export potential of the region.

qa_highlights.question: Growth opportunity and initiatives in air freight?
qa_highlights.answer: Air import and export are both being expanded with carriers on new airport capacity (including Navi Mumbai); export demand is strong, with contractual space agreements and profitability described as good, without figures.

qa_highlights.question: Business mix evolution over 3-5 years, particularly warehousing?
qa_highlights.answer: Warehousing expected to rise from 13-14% to 17-18% and then about 20% of revenue, with investment only where anchor customers exist.

qa_highlights.question: Warehouse strategy: utilisation of existing sites or new leased facilities?
qa_highlights.answer: Current utilisation is about 97.5%; further expansion will be made only if profitable, with racking in existing space paying back in two to three years.

qa_highlights.question: How are geopolitical issues and shipping disruptions affecting demand and volumes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the situation is unpredictable, but new routings are being found; lead and transit times have risen somewhat, though cargo is moving.

qa_highlights.question: How much of revenue growth came from freight rates versus volumes; what drove EBITDA growth of about 90%?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth was largely freight-rate driven; costs are largely fixed for an asset-light model, so margin gains flow to EBITDA; new software and tight control on employment and other operating costs also helped; interest cost rose with working capital.

qa_highlights.question: Expected annualised revenue and profitability from the Bhiwandi expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR50 lakh a year from the 15,000 sq ft; about INR40-50 lakh from pallet positions once occupied; about INR1 crore total at full utilisation. No profitability figure was given.

qa_highlights.question: Growth opportunity in specialised warehousing for e-commerce, quick commerce and FMCG; global partnerships?
qa_highlights.answer: Specialised warehousing is seen as a promising growth area; overseas presence is via the WCA network, and future global presence is planned mainly where the company controls cargo flows.

Interest cost rising with working capital needs as turnover grows.
Geopolitical disruption in the Gulf and other routes is extending transit times.
Bhiwandi occupancy from e-commerce and quick-commerce customers lacks fixed contracts and may fluctuate.
Warehousing share target of 20% depends on continued customer-backed expansion; no capex amount was disclosed for the Bhiwandi works.

504614|2026-03.headline: FY26 consolidated EBITDA rose 44% to INR2,025 crores and PAT 58% to INR1,109 crores, with Q4 PAT up 53% YoY to INR155 crores.
504614|2026-03.overview: Management reported record FY26 thermal (4,155 MU ex-captive, +84% YoY) and hydro (661 MU, +31%) generation, with the energy segment contributing about two-thirds of EBITDA. Consolidated revenue rose 23% to INR5,928 crores, and net debt fell to INR215 crores from INR1,566 crores. Q4 was dented by a 30 MW captive unit shutdown, a 300 MW turbine maintenance outage in January, seasonal hydro slowdown and the coal mine hitting its 1.8 MTPA approved limit. Management outlined a doubling of energy capacity to 1,200 MW by FY30 after the Supreme Court dismissed appeals on the SKS Power acquisition, plus a Raipur pellet expansion to 2 MTPA.

segments.name: Thermal power (ex captive)
segments.commentary: Generation reached a record 4,155 MU in FY26 versus 2,238 MU in FY25 (+84%), helped by SKS Power integration. Around 400 crore sellable units are guided for FY27 versus about 375 crore units sold in FY26; FY26 realisation was above INR5/unit.

segments.name: Hydropower
segments.commentary: Generation hit a record 661 MU in FY26 versus 508 MU in FY25 (+31%), helped by the 25 MW Rehar project. Management said the hydro segment EBITDA was about INR386 crores, and that two hydro projects have long-term PPAs.

segments.name: Steel, sponge iron and pellets
segments.commentary: Iron ore pellet output hit a record 826,293 MT and sponge iron 345,066 MT in FY26; HB wire record 40,425 MT. Steel realisation improved YoY and QoQ in Q4 but FY26 averaged below FY25.

segments.name: Coal mining (Gare Palma IV/7)
segments.commentary: FY26 output hit the 1.8 MTPA permissible limit after CECB consent for expansion from 1.68 MTPA; Q4 volumes were lower as the annual cap was exhausted. Domestic coal sales were about 150k MT, as most output is captively consumed.

guidance_outlook: SKS Power capacity to double to 1,200 MW by FY30; management now says commissioning is around 2030-31 because fresh environment clearance is being sought after the earlier one expired.
Acquisition of a majority stake in Adishankar Khuitam Power (66 MW, Arunachal Pradesh) approved; DPR being finalised, with the project expected to start by end-2026 and take 3-4 years.
Three small Chhattisgarh hydro projects (74 MW in total) may take 3-4 years to commission.
50 MW captive solar expected by end of Q1 FY27 (about September per later remarks); 30 MW TG set replacement to be back by end-June 2026.
Shahpur West high-grade coal mine targeted for commissioning before end-FY27; full-year operations expected in FY28.
Raipur pellet plant expansion from 0.9 to 2.0 MTPA, capex about INR500 crores, completion within 2.5 years; EC in place and DPR under preparation.

Annual hydro capex of about INR500-700 crores; the 600 MW IPP expansion to bring 'full blast' capex from next year, which will be substantially higher. Management did not give an investment figure for SKS expansion yet.
Management is evaluating separation of the renewable energy business (not the full power business); no conclusion yet.
Capex of about INR150 crores over the next two years at the Binjkot plant to improve PLF.
capex_capacity: Gare Palma IV/7 coal mine expansion to 1.8 MTPA with CECB consent; approvals for Gare Palma IV/5, Bartunga and Senduri coal mines progressing.
Binjkot (SKS) plant: over INR140 crores capex invested to date, with about INR150 crores more planned over the next two years to lift PLF.
Raipur pellet plant: 9 lakh tons to 20 lakh tons; about INR500 crores capex; 2.5-year build.
Mineral wool project installed to use industrial waste; management expects it to add to bottom line as it ramps up.
FY27 earnings drivers named: full-year Rehar hydro, efficiency gains at the IPP, 50 MW solar and the 30 MW TG set; FY28 driver is full-year Shahpur coal mine.
demand_pricing: Power exchange prices averaged INR3.75/unit in Q4 FY26, versus INR4.30 a year earlier and INR3.33 in Q3. Peak demand hit a record 270.8 GW.
Indian coal index rose 8% from March 2025 and 9% from December 2025 levels, due to import disruption from the West Asia conflict.

Steel prices recovered by about 10-15% in Q4 FY26 after reaching multi-year lows. Management expects long-product prices to rise once the conflict settles, but would not give Q1 FY27 realisation guidance.
Management said NMDC and OMC have cut iron ore prices, so end-product prices may fall.
India crude steel output grew over 11% in FY26; steel consumption about 164 million tonnes. Safeguard duties have reduced Chinese imports.

About 300 MW of the 600 MW IPP capacity is under PPA (medium/long term), with about 200 MW under PPA this year, rising to 300 MW next year. Management said PPA prices give more visibility than the volatile spot market.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the company restarting steel/pellet capex after holding back for a long time?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited environment clearance and land/water already in place, and expected many Chhattisgarh iron ore mines to open within 2-2.5 years. The Raipur pellet expansion is designed to be ready when they do.

qa_highlights.question: Is there room to improve IPP efficiency and EBITDA per unit?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is scope to improve PLF at Binjkot, with about INR150 crores of capex planned over two years and spares and pending capex being completed.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company demerge steel and power?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said only the renewable energy business is being examined for separation, with no conclusion yet; the full power business is not part of it.

qa_highlights.question: When will the SKS 600 MW doubling be commissioned?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said commissioning is now expected around 2030-31 because fresh environment clearance is being obtained, as the earlier clearance had expired. Capex amount will be given after configuration is frozen.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27-FY28 capex and growth plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Annual hydro capex is about INR500-700 crores, with the 600 MW expansion adding substantially higher capex from next year. FY27 growth comes from efficiency, full-year Rehar, the IPP, solar and TG set; FY28 from full-year Shahpur mine.

qa_highlights.question: What were FY26 sellable units and realisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Previous-year sellable units were about 375 crore units and FY27 is guided to about 400 crore units. Average realisation was more than INR5 per unit.

qa_highlights.question: Why were Godawari Power shares bought in the open market?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called it normal treasury operations with no specific plans. Liquidity is about INR2,400 crores and the stake was about 1% of that.

risks_watch: West Asia conflict: the outcome affects steel, ferro alloy and coal prices, and demand. Management said a renewed war could weaken demand.
Timelines are slipping: SKS doubling is now 2030-31 and the 3 small hydro projects may take 3-4 years. The Chhattisgarh 74 MW and 66 MW Khuitam projects are at DPR and approval stages.
Coal mine output is capped at 1.8 MTPA, so Q4 showed weaker volumes; approvals for other mines are still pending.
Management did not disclose cost of generation or Q1 FY27 steel realisations, and did not give a capex figure for the SKS expansion yet.
Q4 disclosures were inconsistent on the domestic coal sales figure (150k MT) and on EBITDA definitions for the hydro segment.

504614|2026-06.headline: Sarda Energy Q1 FY27 total income INR 1,717 cr, EBITDA INR 762 cr and PAT INR 478 cr (+9.4% YoY), helped by a one-time INR 110 cr net benefit.
504614|2026-06.overview: Management reported record quarterly EBITDA and PAT despite planned shutdowns, unplanned outages and weak small-hydro generation from delayed monsoon. Net profit included a one-time net benefit of INR 110 cr from regulatory approval of the final project cost of the 113 MW Sikkim hydro plant, which management said was worth about INR 162.6 cr of revenue and INR 18 cr of interest income. Energy contributed nearly 70% of consolidated EBITDA, and the company said it is now net debt-free with liquidity above INR 2,500 cr as of 30 June 2026. Metals volumes fell QoQ because of captive power and furnace shutdowns at Raipur, Vizag and Siltara. Management declined to give numerical FY27 guidance.

segments.name: Energy (IPP and captive power)
segments.commentary: Contributed nearly 70% of consolidated EBITDA. Medium and long-term PPAs cover over 380 MW of 710 MW saleable capacity; about 330 MW of these are at SKS, at INR 5-6/unit. Small hydro output was hit by the delayed monsoon, and the company said it is roughly 1% below last year.

segments.name: Sikkim 113 MW hydro
segments.commentary: Shut from 18 June to 5 July 2026 after a transmission tower collapsed in heavy rain and landslide. Management said it is now running at full capacity, with about 5 days of July generation lost and the restoration cost covered by insurance apart from a minimal excess.

segments.name: Steel and ferro alloys (metals)
segments.commentary: Consolidated revenue fell QoQ on planned outages: a 30 MW captive unit replacement at Raipur (trial run now, commercial operation expected mid-August), a 23-day Vizag captive shutdown, and a 53-day Siltara ferro alloy furnace refurbishment. Steel prices were range-bound with a mild negative bias; ferro alloy prices improved modestly.

segments.name: Mineral wool (new)
segments.commentary: Running at about 60-65% of capacity, with production constrained by imported equipment held up by the West Asia crisis. Management said the project is not yet profitable, and it expects FY27 revenue of INR 90-110 cr.

segments.name: Mining (coal)
segments.commentary: Shahpur West is due to commission before end-FY27 (0.6 Mt). Bartunga Hill (2.1 Mt) is due by end-FY28. Gare Palma IV/5 (2.0 Mt), Gare Palma IV/7 (1.8 Mt) and Senduri (0.6 Mt, provisional) make up the mining plan; the target is 7.1 Mt capacity.

guidance_outlook: No numerical FY27 PAT or EBITDA guidance; management said the company does not give forward profitability figures and that the market is volatile.
Q2 expected to be better than Q1, driven by hydro generation and higher power prices. July IEX prices were about INR 5/unit versus INR 4.19-4.20 a year earlier.
FY27 IPP generation expected to exceed last year's 415 crore units, with the captive plant utilisation also improving after the 30 MW unit restarts.
Steel and ferro alloy prices expected to remain stable. Ferro alloy margins may firm as raw material prices soften; steel may rise after a West Asia settlement and after monsoon.
Real power tariffs expected at INR 5-6/unit for the year, rising with inflation and peak demand, especially for hydro.

Full-year FY27 pipeline: 50 MW captive solar expected by end of next quarter (after a railway right-of-way delay); 74 MW Chhattisgarh small hydro approvals on schedule; Arunachal 66 MW hydro detailed engineering to begin this year.

SKS 600 MW to 1,200 MW expansion: TOR submission in about 3 months, then public hearing and 6-8 months for EC, then 6-8 months to appoint a consultant. The new unit is targeted for FY31 completion (per management, asked on the last call).
capex_capacity: SKS thermal expansion from 600 MW to 1,200 MW is awaiting regulatory approval, and the company describes the brownfield project as capital-efficient, using existing land, water and evacuation infrastructure.
Waste heat recovery power plant at Vizag, about INR 300 cr, for energy efficiency; all expansion projects funded through internal accruals.

Coal mining: Shahpur West commissioning before end-FY27; Bartunga Hill by end of next financial year; Gare Palma IV/5, IV/7 and Senduri approvals in progress. Management said the Gare Palma IV/7 expansion from 1.8 Mt to 5 Mt is not in the immediate plan as new higher-grade mines take priority.
Shahpur West coal is high grade and is destined for sponge iron and ferro alloy plants, not the power plants.
Plans to quadruple mining capacity and double energy generation capacity, per management.
demand_pricing: India power generation grew 9.4% YoY to about 523 BU in the quarter; thermal grew 7.5%; solar generation rose about 45%; small hydro fell about 30% and large hydro about 7%.
Day-ahead market averaged INR 3.85/unit vs INR 3.92 a year earlier, but July prices rose to about INR 5/unit from INR 4.19. Management said peak hours have lengthened from 5 to 8-10 hours.
Indian coal index for June 2026 was about 21% above June 2025 and about 11% above March 2026.
India crude steel output grew over 7.5% in H1 CY26; imports exceeded exports again after two quarters. Management welcomed anti-dumping investigations.
West Asia conflict is raising input costs and creating supply chain issues. Management called the impact manageable but is in a wait-and-watch stance.

financial_highlights.change: Highest ever quarterly EBITDA per management

financial_highlights.metric: One-time net benefit in PAT (Sikkim final project cost approval)
financial_highlights.change: Approx. INR 162.6 cr revenue and INR 18 cr other income pre-tax; about 25% of INR 110 cr at EBITDA level per CFO

financial_highlights.value: More than INR 2,500 cr as of 30 June 2026

qa_highlights.question: Is realisation per unit falling as more PPAs are signed, given the implied ~INR 8/unit on power sales?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the back-calculated realisation is wrong because current income includes prior-year adjustments. Full-year power should be assumed at INR 5-6/unit, rising with inflation and peak demand, especially for hydro.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 110 cr one-time benefit's P&L split available, and what is the other-income effect?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue impact was about INR 162.64 cr and other income about INR 18 cr (interest awarded with tariff). EBITDA effect is about 25% of the INR 110 cr, net of tax.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the 380 MW of PPAs is at SKS, what tariff applies, and what is the maximum SKS PPA quantity?
qa_highlights.answer: About 330 MW of the 380 MW is at SKS, at INR 5-6/unit. Maximum SKS quantity is 540 MW, and management said it still has to decide how far to commit.

qa_highlights.question: Which coal mines make up the 7.1 Mt target, and is Gare Palma IV/7 expansion to 5 Mt planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Gare Palma IV/7 is 1.8 Mt, Shahpur West 0.6 Mt, Senduri about 0.6 Mt (provisional), and Gare Palma IV/5 about 2.0 Mt. Management said the 1.8 to 5 Mt expansion is not in the immediate plan as new higher-grade mines take priority.

qa_highlights.question: What is the SKS 600 MW to 1,200 MW environmental clearance timeline and construction start?
qa_highlights.answer: TOR submission in about 3 months, then public hearing and 6-8 months for EC, then 6-8 months to appoint a consultant before procedures start. Management did not give a construction start date.

qa_highlights.question: When will the new SKS unit be completed, and will turnover more than double?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated completion by FY31, as stated on the last call. On turnover doubling, management said it should be by that time.

qa_highlights.question: Has Sikkim hydro normalised, and is there residual Q2 impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Sikkim is operating at full capacity. Management does not expect a residual impact in Q2, apart from about 5 days of July generation lost.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY27 PAT and EBITDA be guided numerically?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management said it does not give forward profitability guidance given the volatile market. It said Q2 should be better on hydro and July power prices, and FY27 IPP generation should exceed last year's 415 crore units.

qa_highlights.question: What is the mineral wool revenue, and what are the Q2 and FY27 sales and EBITDA targets?
qa_highlights.answer: Plant is at 60-65% of capacity and not yet profitable. Management guided FY27 revenue of about INR 90-110 cr, said Q2 is hard to comment on, and expects full production in about 6 months.

risks_watch: Delayed monsoon and hydro generation: small hydro was about 1% below last year in Q1, and Q2 depends on rainfall.
Mineral wool ramp-up: capacity at 60-65%, with imported equipment stuck due to the West Asia crisis; the project is loss-making.

Regulatory timing: SKS 600 MW to 1,200 MW EC needs TOR, public hearing and 6-8 months; Arunachal and Chhattisgarh approvals and 50 MW solar commissioning depend on railway right-of-way (1-2 months expected).
Coal mine ramp-up: Shahpur West due before end-FY27, Bartunga Hill by end-FY28; Gare Palma IV/7 expansion not in immediate plan.
West Asia conflict: input cost inflation and supply chain disruption; steel prices hinge on a settlement. Solar daytime oversupply could weigh on day-time power prices, with BESS expected to offset.
Quality of earnings: Q1 PAT included a one-time INR 110 cr net benefit, and the company gave no numerical FY27 guidance.
key_quotes: Q1 FY '27 stands as testament to the series of decisions we have taken over the last few years to build a diversified integrated business model, one that has continued to help us navigate external challenges.

We are now net debt -free on both a stand -alone and consolidated basis with a strong balance sheet and healthy liquidity of more than INR 2,500 crores as of 30th June 2026, giving us significant flexibility to execute our long-term growth plans.

504973|2026-06.headline: Chola MS Q1 FY27 combined ratio rose to 120.4% with GWP up 6.7% to Rs 2,130 crore and motor OD loss ratio still elevated.
504973|2026-06.overview: Chola MS (general insurance arm of Cholamandalam Financial Holdings) reported GDPI of Rs 1,860 crore (+2.6% YoY) and GWP of Rs 2,130 crore (+6.7%), below management's expectations. Claims ratio rose to 85.6% (vs 81.3%) and combined ratio to 120.4%, driven by motor reserve strengthening, elevated motor OD claims and a large fire loss (Rs 12.4 crore net). Profit before tax was Rs 116 crore on operating profit of Rs 71 crore. Management said the OD loss ratio is unacceptable and targets a high-70s level first, while the Supreme Court motor TP (homemaker) judgment remains unprovided pending review.

segments.name: Commercial lines
segments.commentary: Portfolio declined 8.6% in Q1 vs industry fire decline of ~28%; Chola MS fire decline limited to 15.5%. Growth in marine, engineering and liability.

segments.name: Health

505192|2026-03.headline: SML Mahindra FY26 revenue rose 18% and PAT 31%, but Q4 PAT grew only 2% on a 16% revenue rise as commodity inflation hit.
505192|2026-03.overview: This was the first investor call since Mahindra's 58.96% controlling acquisition completed on 1 August 2025, about eight months post-takeover. Management said FY26 volumes grew 28% in cargo and 12% in passenger vehicles, with market share up 20 bps in cargo and 80 bps in passenger for the full year. Q4 showed a cargo share dip, which management attributed to pre-poned institutional orders executed in Q3, while bus share gained 170 bps in the quarter. Q4 commodity inflation was about 1.3% of cost (roughly 3.5-3.7% annualised), and a price increase of about 2-3% was taken from 15 April 2026.

financial_highlights.change: up two notches from AA minus

segments.name: Cargo (trucks)
segments.commentary: FY26 volume up 28% with market share up 20 bps for the year; Q4 cargo share declined, attributed by management to Q3 pre-ponement of institutional orders. Q4 cargo volume grew 10%.

segments.name: Passenger (buses)
segments.commentary: FY26 volume up 12% with market share up 80 bps; Q4 bus share gained 170 bps in the peak school-bus season. Q4 passenger volume grew 16%.

guidance_outlook: Management aspires to a top-three position in India's ILCV trucks and buses segment, with focus on HCVs, and targets 10-12% combined market share by FY31 (currently about 6%).
Around FY31, the company targets about Rs 15,000 crore revenue, per the Global Investor Day, against a 3.5-tonne-plus revenue pool of about Rs 1.25 lakh crore last year.
Q1 FY27 plans are largely unchanged from original plans as of the call; management said a diesel price increase is the key swing factor.

Commodity inflation is expected to be partly temporary; management said price increases and commodity hedges should largely cover headwinds, and inflation is not expected to persist through FY27 if the Middle East situation eases.
First EV bus is to be launched in FY27; management gave no capex or volume figures for it.
A longer-format strategy session is planned for July 2026, close to the AGM.
capex_capacity: Service network: combined touchpoints to rise from about 300 to 450 by pooling 150 service setups across both brands; 70 are operational and 80 more are due by end of Q1 FY27.

Engineering and manufacturing synergies are being pursued to reduce product cost and capex outlay, including sharing engine (4-valve diesel and CNG 3.8-litre) and ADAS development with Mahindra teams.
ADAS regulation compliance (due in about 1.5 years) is a joint project with Mahindra, with cost detail deferred to launch.
EV bus development is underway; management said capex for scale-up will depend on market evolution.
demand_pricing: Industry grew about 2% in H1 FY26 and about 22% in H2 post-GST reform; ICV trucks +42%, LCV trucks +20%, MCV trucks +28%, ILCV +8% in that period.
Management sees no demand deferment yet and cites pent-up replacement demand, though a diesel price hike and Middle East disruption could moderate demand.
Q4 commodity inflation was about 1.3% of cost; Q1 FY27 saw further increases in some commodities (steel, aluminium, copper, polymers, gases), with some volatility.
Price increases of about 2% (some 3%) on SML products effective 15 April 2026; more may follow based on analysis.
Electric bus industry share is below 1% of the segment; private buyers are not yet buying e-buses beyond STU purchases.

qa_highlights.question: What is the industry outlook, market share trajectory and synergy timing?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 industry shifted from about 2% growth in H1 to about 22% in H2. Management said synergies come on both the back end (sourcing, engineering, manufacturing) and the front end (common dealers in unrepresented territories), with growth as the main thesis.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a plan to merge the two companies or delist SML?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no delisting plan. On a merger, it is working on long-term strategy and will update at the right time.

qa_highlights.question: What are the supply chain and cost impacts of the current crisis?
qa_highlights.answer: No vehicle production was lost through Q4 despite gas, aluminium and polymer shortages. Steel, aluminium, copper and polymers rose, and gases trade at a premium; management expects most increases to be temporary.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ADAS cost impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called ADAS a significant development and said cost and detail would be shared at launch.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any demand deferment seen in March or April?
qa_highlights.answer: No deferment as of now; peak school-bus season is underway and Q1 plans are largely as originally planned, but management flagged diesel price risk.

qa_highlights.question: What was the Q4 margin headwind and what pricing offset is planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 inflation was about 1.3% of cost (about 3.5-3.7% annualised). Price increases of about 2-3% began 15 April, and hedges will provide a partial offset, though steel cannot be hedged. Management said pricing should largely cover headwinds.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EV bus and e-mobility strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: The first EV bus launches in FY27 with product details to follow closer to launch. Capex scale-up will depend on market evolution, as private buyers are not yet buying e-buses.

risks_watch: Diesel price increase and Middle East disruption could moderate CV demand after Q1 FY27.
Commodity inflation (steel, aluminium, copper, polymers, gases) may persist; hedges do not cover steel, and pricing actions may lag.
Q4 PAT growth of 2% vs revenue growth of 16% indicates margin pressure that must be tracked in Q1 FY27.
Cargo market share dip in Q4 FY26 tied to order timing; watch whether share recovers in FY27.
Integration delivery: service network expansion to 450 touchpoints and cross-badging, plus dealer-channel sensitivity.
Timing and scope of the July 2026 strategy session and merger-related updates.

key_quotes: We have outgrown the industry. We grew at 17% in the industry versus industry growth of 13%.

505196|2026-06.headline: TIL Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 86% YoY to INR117.1 crore, with EBITDA margin at 6.2% (vs 1.5%) and PAT at negative INR5.5 crore.
505196|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue of INR117.1 crore included Tulip Compression (TCPL) only from 8 May to 30 June 2026, so the quarter is a partial-period read. Standalone revenue grew 25% YoY to INR78.6 crore, with EBITDA up to INR3.4 crore (4.3% margin vs 1.5%), but standalone PAT was negative INR7.2 crore. Management flagged that blended margins will stay volatile for the next six to eight quarters because of product mix and supply-chain localisation, and gave no near-term margin guidance. The company delivered nine ReachStackers and reported a current order book of INR211 crore against a pipeline of about INR373 crore.

segments.commentary: Revenue INR78.6 crore (+25% YoY), EBITDA margin 4.3%. Management said FY26 turnover was about 50% defence. Nine ReachStackers delivered in the quarter.

segments.commentary: Consolidated from 8 May 2026 (part period). Order book INR328 crore, pipeline INR117 crore. FY26 revenue about INR278 crore per management. Management's medium-to-long-term EBITDA margin view is 14-15%.

segments.commentary: FY26 aftermarket about INR56 crore. Management's long-term aim is 40-45% of revenue; parts margins 25-35%, service margins slightly better.

qa_highlights.answer: Share is 38-40%, and the CONCOR order is one-time. Management expects ReachStacker sales to scale to a sizable number this year via retail and niche buyers.

qa_highlights.question: Can the current order book deliver more than INR200 crore this year?

505200|2026-06.headline: Eicher Motors Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 32% to INR 6,632 crore with record Royal Enfield volumes of 332,940 units.
505200|2026-06.overview: Eicher Motors posted its best-ever Q1 with consolidated revenue of INR 6,632 crore (up 32% YoY), EBITDA of INR 1,591 crore and PAT of INR 1,463 crore (up 21%). 505283|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 sales rose 21% to INR706 crore and FY26 PBT hit a record INR356 crore, but management flags 18-20% EBITDA as sustainable, not the 21.7% delivered.

FY26 EBITDA was INR388 crore (21.7% of total income) and PBT INR356 crore (19.6%), supported by in-house backward integration and a selective order-acceptance stance. The unexecuted order board rose 15% to INR1,863 crore as of April 1, 2026, including Precision Components, and the company remains debt-free with about INR460 crore net cash. Management called FY26's margin an exception and guided to 18-20% EBITDA going forward, while reaffirming a 20%+ growth aspiration.
