505533|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue rose 9% YoY to INR 6.6 billion and same-store sales grew 1.5%, driven by mid-single-digit guest count growth, with positive footfall in all three months and momentum continuing into April. Full-year revenue grew 5% to INR 26.3 billion. Gross margin held near historic highs at 68.1% (up about 60 bps QoQ), and full-year cash PAT was INR 2.4 billion (9% of sales). Management said it is too early to call a sustained revival, and it guided to 60+ restaurant openings in FY27 versus a record 48 in FY26.

financial_highlights.change: About +60 bps QoQ; near historic highs

segments.name: West region
segments.commentary: Management described West as the strongest growth driver, though it was affected by LPG disruptions; no specific West SSS figure was given.

segments.name: South region
segments.commentary: Same-store sales ended the quarter nearly flat, a meaningful improvement on prior quarters, with guest count turning marginally positive after the company rolled back to everyday value (except Chennai, where it is a trial).

segments.name: Digital and delivery (McDelivery, app)
segments.commentary: Cumulative app downloads crossed 52 million with about 3.5 million monthly active users growing at double-digit YoY; delivery grew about 6% vs dine-in about 9%.

guidance_outlook: Open 60+ restaurants annually going forward (FY27), with all new stores fully digital-equipped and including McCafés; Vision 2027 target of 580-630 restaurants retained.
Gross margin in the near term indicated at around 67% or higher, reflecting current inflation partly offset by cost optimisation.
Price increases of 2-4% a year are the policy, but none taken in the last four to five months and no immediate plan; some small increases possible.

Vision 2027 target: first reach about INR 3,000 crore in sales; Ind AS EBITDA margin improvement to 13-15% expected mainly from operating leverage, with a breakup for the next two years to be given closer to FY27 start.
Aim to lift SSSG towards mid-single digits as early as possible.
Toys for Happy Meals expected to take about 9 to 12 months to return; books being used meanwhile.
Store closures of about 6-7 a year expected as part of portfolio management.
capex_capacity: Opened a record 48 restaurants in FY26, with 21 in Q4, taking the total to 478 restaurants across 78 cities.
Plan to open 60+ restaurants annually; partnerships with HPCL, BPCL and Jio-bp to expand highway footprint, plus airports, malls and six key metros.
Store closures in FY26 were about 6-7, attributed to malls shutting, highway access changes and lease tenure; management said this is not South-specific.
Store modernisation investment helped resilience: all restaurants operational, with fewer than 10% on limited menu due to LPG shortages.
demand_pricing: Q4 SSSG of 1.5% came with mid-single-digit guest count growth; management said it would not break out the Navratri and LPG effects, and that around 10% of stores were hit by LPG shortages from 10 March.
Growth is being driven by the 99 everyday value meal, with McCafé subscription (10 coffees a month for INR 55) and merchandise campaigns (sipper, tote bag) aimed at Gen Z.
Commodity pressure: cocoa and coffee inflation in FY26, offset by supply chain efficiencies and contract timing; management said last year's inflation tailwind may not repeat.
Management said it would hold product-mix margin dilution where it is and is not planning further value price cuts beyond current levels.

qa_highlights.question: What is the normalised SSG for Q4 after Navratri timing and supply disruptions?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to adjust further and said 1.5% SSSG is the number, with mid-single-digit guest count growth; momentum of 8-10% growth is seen in recent weeks.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the gross margin expanding and what is FY27 pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: Supply chain initiatives and an internal cost project offset inflation; FY26 inflation was a tailwind that may not repeat. Pricing policy is 2-4% a year, but no price increase has been taken for four to five months and none is planned.

qa_highlights.question: Why is store opening guidance 60+ versus the usual 40-50, and why the closures?
qa_highlights.answer: The 60+ number reflects Vision 2027 (580-630 restaurants) and penetration headroom; closures are portfolio management of about 6-7 a year and were not South-specific.

qa_highlights.question: Will the expansion target hold if the LPG and raw material pressure persists for six months?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is confident the store target holds, citing cost levers and industry-wide price increases as options if inflation rises.

qa_highlights.question: What is the health and protein-led consumer read?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the mid-single-digit guest count growth shows no health-driven issue; it cited the Aloo Tikki balanced meal, lower sodium fries, reduced mayo fat, protein slice and millet bun as menu choices.

risks_watch: LPG shortages and geopolitical-driven commodity inflation (cocoa, coffee, supplier costs) could pressure gross margin below the 67% indication.
Delivery growth (about 6%) lags dine-in (about 9%); management wants equal growth from both channels.
Toy supply for Happy Meals still blocked by the BIS issue for about 9-12 months.
Store closures expected at 6-7 a year; whether the FY27 60+ opening pace is achieved.
SSSG remains only 1.5%, well below the mid-single-digit target; management would not call it a sustained revival.
505533|2026-03.management_tone: Cautious-to-confident: management stressed that the revival is early and that the company will not call it sustained until more quarters show consistent momentum. Management was evasive on the sub-components of SSSG, on the Navratri effect and on the opex bps question, which it deferred offline.
key_quotes: Despite the challenges, we delivered a steady performance underpinned by improving guest count trends and sustained profitability.
we would refrain from calling this a sustained revival until we see a few more quarters and months of consistent momentum.
Value is not difficult in a current environment to get, but we wanted to really, really focus on volume.
We reap what we sow.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Gross margin at 68.1% in Q4 (about +60 bps QoQ) and 67.7% for FY26 (about +140 bps YoY); management indicates 67% or higher near term, and Ind AS EBITDA margin to 13-15% under Vision 2027 via operating leverage, but FY26 operating EBITDA margin was flat at 13.2% and management flagged commodity and LPG inflation and that last year's tailwind may not repeat.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Record 48 openings in FY26 (21 in Q4) took the base to 478 restaurants, and management has guided to 60+ openings in FY27 with named HPCL, BPCL and Jio-bp highway partnerships plus airports, malls and six metros; Vision 2027 target of 580-630 restaurants is retained.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Q4 same-store sales grew 1.5% on mid-single-digit guest count growth, with momentum of 8-10% growth seen in recent weeks and positive footfall in all three months; but management said it is too early to call a sustained revival and delivery (about 6%) lags dine-in (about 9%).

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is not disclosed, and the 60+ openings plan with Vision 2027 target of 580-630 restaurants already sets the capex envelope, so a fresh capex announcement is only a possibility; the breakup of the next two years is to be given closer to FY27 start.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: SSSG is only 1.5% versus the mid-single-digit aim, management declined to call the revival sustained, and the 2-4% price policy has not been applied for four to five months with no immediate plan.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Gross margin indication of around 67% or higher could be pressured by cocoa, coffee and LPG-driven inflation (about 10% of stores hit by LPG shortages from 10 March), and Happy Meal toy supply remains blocked for 9-12 months.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Management is pushing the 99 everyday value meal, McCafé subscription (10 coffees for INR 55) and merchandise campaigns, and all new stores will include McCafés, but no specific new menu launch date was given; Happy Meal toys are expected to return in 9-12 months.

rows.label: Price increases of 2-4% a year as policy, none taken for 4-5 months
rows.why: Policy is 2-4% annually, but no increase has been taken in four to five months and no immediate plan exists; only small increases are possible, so realisation is uncertain while inflation persists.

rows.label: SSSG aim to lift towards mid-single digits
rows.why: Q4 SSSG was 1.5% with South nearly flat after rolling back to everyday value, and the Happy Meal toy supply is blocked for 9-12 months, so a move to mid-single digits depends on sustained guest count growth.

rows.label: Store closures of 6-7 a year
rows.why: Management expects 6-7 closures a year as portfolio management (malls shutting, highway access changes, lease tenure), which trims the net addition from the 60+ gross openings.

tone.note: Management was confident on the 60+ restaurant opening pace, the Vision 2027 target and the 67%+ gross margin, but cautious that the SSSG revival is early and it would not call it sustained; it was evasive on the SSSG sub-components, the Navratri effect and opex bps, which it deferred offline.

505533|2026-06.headline: Westlife Foodworld Q1 FY27 revenue rose 12% YoY to INR 7.36 billion with SSSG of 4.3%, though operating EBITDA margin was broadly stable amid inflation.
505533|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue hit a record INR 7.36 billion, up 12% YoY, with same-store sales growth of 4.3% and positive SSSG in all three months. Growth was guest-count led, with double-digit footfall growth and the South turning SSSG-positive. Operating EBITDA rose 11% YoY to INR 946 million, but the operating EBITDA margin was broadly stable as over 200 bps of inflation (fuel, food, packaging, utilities, labour) was absorbed. Management said Q1 marks the peak of gross margin pressure and expects improvement from here, while restaurant additions were only 5 in the quarter.

financial_highlights.change: Positive in all three months; May and June mid-single-digit

segments.name: West
segments.commentary: Management described West as continuing to deliver a very strong performance, with growth aided by a rollout of the value platform and expanded store clusters in Gujarat, Pune/rest of Maharashtra and Mumbai (each ~100 restaurants).

segments.name: South
segments.commentary: South ended the quarter with positive SSSG and double-digit guest count in all three months; management cited close to 4.5% SSSG this quarter. South has more than half of the store base per management, and Bangalore has 60+ restaurants, Hyderabad 35+ and Chennai 20+.

guidance_outlook: Over 60 new restaurants in FY27, reiterated as on track; 580 to 630 restaurants by December 2027 (Vision 2027).

Management expects some cost pressures to ease as geopolitical conditions improve; targets 100-150 bps YoY improvement in pre-Ind AS EBITDA margin as an internal long-term guidance, and aspires to 100+ bps expansion in FY27 (FY26 pre-Ind AS margin cited as 7.6%).
Mid-single-digit SSSG confidence for the year, with South expected to reach mid-single-digit; management declined to give high-single-digit targets.
G&A expected at 6% to 6.5% of sales for the remaining year.
Interim dividend of INR 0.40 per equity share approved by the Board.
No price increase taken yet in FY27; annual price increase guidance is around 3%, to be taken later after consumer research.
risks_watch: Operating EBITDA margin only stable despite 11% EBITDA growth; inflation in fuel, food, packaging, utilities and labour could persist if geopolitical conditions do not ease.
Store additions of 5 in Q1 versus 60+ guided for FY27; the back-ended ramp is needed to reach 580 to 630 by December 2027.
Lower historic store economics and margin trend questioned by analysts over five to seven years; management declined to engage on the data.
Sustainability of SSSG momentum beyond Q1, and the reliance on guest-count growth while ticket growth remains weak.
Management reliance on deferred price increases (none taken yet) to protect margins.
505533|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on volume momentum and recovery in South, but cautious and non-committal on specific forward numbers (SSSG, margin path, multi-year EBITDA). Management repeatedly framed FY27 margin expansion as aspirational and avoided detailed guidance.
key_quotes: Q1 FY27 marks our strongest topline growth, highest same -store sales growth and fastest guest count growth in the recent past.
We haven't done any price increase yet.
So we are on track to deliver our guidance of 580 to 630 restaurants as per Vision 2027.

qa_highlights.question: Does current momentum give comfort to reach the FY27 topline target of INR 30 billion?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said momentum is sustainable and is building on the strategy launched last year, with the first positive guest-count SSSG in October to December. It said it needs to be close to 15%-plus growth to meet Vision 2027 and believes it is on track.

qa_highlights.question: Will EBITDA margins expand with 4.5-5% SSSG, and what is the FY29 margin target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the inflation was unbudgeted and largely from fuel, packaging and marketing spend, and it is not structural. It gave 100-150 bps YoY improvement as an internal long-term guidance and declined to give a two-to-three-year target, citing levers in product mix, cost engineering, bottom-performing stores and pricing.

qa_highlights.question: Is 100-150 bps pre-Ind AS margin expansion in FY27 formal guidance or aspiration?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is working towards 100 bps-plus expansion over FY26's pre-Ind AS margin of 7.6%, and that it is in Vision 2027 as an accountable goal, not formal guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Is Q1 the peak of gross margin pressure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 is the highest level of impact and margins should improve from here, with operating margin being the focus. Inflation came from fuel, food, paper and distribution, utilities (gas) and labour (minimum wages), with diesel affecting distribution.

qa_highlights.question: What is the G&A run-rate for the rest of the year?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said G&A should be in the range of 6% to 6.5% of sales, and the focus should be on the bottom line rather than individual expense lines.

qa_highlights.question: Why were only 5 restaurants opened in Q1 against 60+ guided for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there was a short inventory gap because LPG restaurants were converted using electric fryers already in stock during the LPG crisis, so it is a timing issue. It remains confident of 60 openings in FY27.

capex_capacity: Restaurant network at 482 across 79 cities after 5 openings in Q1 FY27; management reiterated over 60 new restaurants in FY27 and 580 to 630 restaurants by December 2027 (Vision 2027).

Store additions were slow in Q1 because of an inventory gap: some LPG restaurants were converted using electric fryers already in inventory during the LPG crisis, which management said is a timing issue.
Last year the company opened more stores in the West and tapered openings in the South while fixing value and execution there; management said the South will see more store openings going forward.

Clusters now include about 100 restaurants each in Gujarat, Pune and rest of Maharashtra, and Mumbai; Bangalore has 60+, Hyderabad 35+ and Chennai 20+ restaurants; South has more than half the store base.
Management said the pipeline remains healthy and that it follows a prudent, profitability-led approach focused on site quality, payback period and long-term store economics.
demand_pricing: Consolidated revenue INR 7.36 billion, up 12% YoY; SSSG 4.3% with positive comps in all three months; May and June at mid-single-digit SSSG and July exit momentum carried forward.

Growth was guest-count led with double-digit footfall in all three months; on-premise sales up 12% YoY and off-premise up 11% YoY; digital contribution 74%, up about 150 bps YoY; delivery share flat to down about 1% per management.

South ended the quarter with positive SSSG and close to 4.5% SSSG for the quarter; management expects mid-single-digit SSSG for the year with growth broad-based, and declined to give region-level or high-single-digit forecasts.
No price increase taken in FY27 so far; management's usual practice is about 3% annual price increase taken gradually, after consumer research.
Ticket growth lagged footfall: management said ticket improvement started to show in Q1, after being far lower in January to March, with December 2025 cited as the inflection point.

505533|2026-09.headline: Westlife Foodworld Q2 FY27 revenue rose 16% to INR7.47 billion, with same-store sales up 10.1% on double-digit guest count growth.
505533|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 was the company's strongest quarter in 13 quarters, with revenue up 16% YoY to INR7.47 billion and same-store sales growth of 10.1%, driven mainly by guest count growth that was double-digit in each month. Operating EBITDA rose 29% YoY (management also cited about 26% in one answer), with margin up 130 bps to 13.1% despite about 190 bps of inflation across commodities, utilities and employee costs. The company opened 11 restaurants, taking the network to 492 across 80 cities, and reiterated its 580+ restaurant target by March 2028. Management said momentum continued into October, and guided to 100-150 bps of annual profitability improvement and 2-4% price increases over the year.

segments.name: On-premise (dine-in)
segments.commentary: Grew 17% YoY in Q2 FY27, similar in pace to off-premise per management.

segments.name: Off-premise (delivery and takeaway)
segments.commentary: Grew 15% YoY; company says delivery is broad-based and in double-digit growth, with own-channel delivery trial in Mumbai.

segments.name: Digital
segments.commentary: Over 75% of sales; 58 million+ cumulative app downloads and about 4.2 million monthly active users.

guidance_outlook: Profitability: maintain 100-150 bps YoY margin improvement guidance for the year, excluding unforeseen shocks; management said the guidance holds despite Karnataka minimum wage increases and higher oil costs.
Pricing: 2-4% weighted average price increase over the year (around 3% typical), versus roughly 2% taken in each of the last couple of years; no large one-time hike planned.
Capex: total FY27 capex INR250-300 crore; per-store cost INR3-3.5 crore.
Expansion: 60-65 restaurants per year; 580+ restaurants by March 2028.
Trading: October momentum continued; management aspires to maintain high single-digit growth as a minimum, though it avoided formal forward-looking statements.
capex_capacity: Opened 11 restaurants in Q2 FY27, taking the total to 492 across 80 cities; 500th restaurant due the following week.
Plan of 60-65 new restaurants per year; target of 580+ by March 2028.
Capex per store INR3-3.5 crore; FY27 capex INR250-300 crore, with cost pressure from USD, duties and technology costs.
Own delivery rider fleet brought back in-house; Mumbai quick-delivery initiative to be scaled only after cost model is understood.
demand_pricing: Guest count grew double digits in each month of Q2; management says growth came from both new or returning customers (lapsed 6+ months) and higher frequency, per survey data.
Same-store sales growth of 10.1%; management said the 3% like-for-like average unit volume figure was a separate trailing-12-month data point and not comparable.
Value platform centred on INR99 entry meal, GMALite and partner discounts; management said discounting was reduced, not increased, and that no extra discount was given vs prior quarters.
Gap between South and West growth is narrowing per management, with strengthened South operating structure; IT-hub areas (Bangalore, Hyderabad) grew in line with West.
Inflation of about 190 bps across commodities, utilities and employee costs; management says price increases absorb roughly half of inflation as a principle.

qa_highlights.question: Promotional intensity and ad spend YoY?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not quantify; said value is a platform, discounting was reduced, and no extra discounts were given versus prior quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 3-4% price hike mean 190 bps of margin gain?
qa_highlights.answer: Not directly; price increases absorb about half of inflation, with cost-saving initiatives also in play, and guidance remains 100-150 bps annual margin improvement.

qa_highlights.question: Can the SSSG trajectory continue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects value interventions and new consumer activations to keep guest count growth going, though it did not give a numeric forecast.

qa_highlights.question: Is the gap between SSSG and guest count closing, and what drives check size?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the guest count momentum since December is the priority; check size is easier to lift, and price contributed little from Q1 to Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Latika Chopra: Is 100-150 bps margin guidance applicable to FY27 given first-half gains?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, management reaffirmed 100-150 bps for this year, citing Karnataka minimum wage hikes and oil costs but a mitigation plan and volume-led negotiating leverage.

qa_highlights.question: How is the 10% SSSG constructed, and what is capex per store and FY capex?
qa_highlights.answer: No further breakup of SSSG; per-store capex INR3-3.5 crore; FY27 capex INR250-300 crore rather than the INR300 crore figure floated.

risks_watch: Sustainability of double-digit guest count growth beyond the current festive season, given that management says value-led growth can fade over two or three quarters.
Input cost inflation: Karnataka minimum wage hike, edible oil and other commodities, and USD-linked capex costs.
Limited disclosure on promotional intensity and ad spend makes it hard to isolate the effect of value discounting on margins.
Delivery trajectory: own-channel delivery expansion beyond Mumbai pending cost model; SSSG split by channel not disclosed.
Restaurant rollout of 60-65 a year needs to hold to reach 580+ by March 2028.

505537|2026-03.headline: Zee Q4 FY26: digital revenue up 71% YoY to INR4,700 mn and ZEE5 EBITDA positive for FY26, but ad revenue fell 4% on a March West Asia hit and a INR4,084 mn one-off charge.
505537|2026-03.overview: Management reported that ZEE5 revenue grew 71% YoY to INR4,700 million in Q4 FY26, its highest ever, and that digital delivered positive EBITDA for FY26 versus a loss of INR5,480 million a year earlier. Linear advertising revenue declined 4% YoY as advertisers pulled spends in March amid the Middle East conflict; management said it would have been low single-digit growth excluding March. A one-off charge of INR4,084 million from a change in movie rights amortization (front-loaded to 50% over two years) and additional impairment was taken in the quarter, and the adjusted EBITDA margin was 6.9% on a 7% decline in operating revenue. Management gave no formal guidance, and the call was mainly Q&A on Zee Music, Bullet, live events, ad spend and manpower costs.

financial_highlights.change: vs loss of INR5,480 million in FY25

financial_highlights.metric: One-off amortization change and impairment, Q4
Other sales and services, Q4 FY26
Content inventory, advances and deposits, Mar-26

financial_highlights.value: INR27.6 billion (cash INR7.5bn, FDs/treasury INR7.8bn, mutual funds INR12.3bn)

segments.name: Digital (ZEE5)
segments.commentary: Revenue up 71% YoY in Q4 to INR4,700 million, the highest ever for the segment; more than 120 shows and movies released including 34 originals across 7 languages. Management said it is operationally profitable and expects momentum to continue in the medium term.

segments.name: Broadcast / Linear TV
segments.commentary: Advertising revenue fell 4% YoY in Q4 as March spends were held back; Zee TV GRPs grew 40% and the Hindi GEC claims prime-time leadership. Network share 17.4% in Q4, above 18% exiting March.

segments.name: Music
segments.commentary: Over 217 billion total video views and more than 176 million YouTube subscribers in FY26 from a catalogue of over 20,000 songs; management called profitability healthy but gave no revenue disclosure.

segments.name: Studios
segments.commentary: Released 13 movies in Q4 (9 own productions, 4 distribution deals); syndication was strong but Studio sales and services fell 47% YoY in Q4.

segments.name: New initiatives (Bullet, CORE, Phantom)
segments.commentary: Board approved INR20 crore investment in CORE Pvt Ltd (live events) and up to INR116 crore in listed VFX firm Phantom Digital Effects Ltd. Bullet micro-drama app is growing but its potential is still being evaluated.

Management aims to bring people cost back toward about 9% of revenue, the pre-pandemic level.
Ad environment expected to stay challenging in the near term while the West Asia crisis continues; medium-term view positive.
ZEE5 aspiration is an ad-to-subscription revenue mix of about 50:50 in the medium term.

505700|2026-06.headline: Elecon Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 11.9% YoY to INR521 crore, but management guided only low double-digit FY27 growth on raw-material-driven order conversion delays.
505700|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations grew 11.9% YoY to INR521 crore over adjusted Q1 FY26 revenue of INR465 crore, with EBITDA up 3.9% to INR109 crore at a stated 21% margin and PAT of INR70 crore (13.5% margin, up 2.3%). Gear division drove growth, with revenue up 16.3% to INR416 crore, while MHE revenue fell 2.9% to INR105 crore on project execution delays and EBIT fell 25.3% to INR27 crore. Order intake rose 23% to INR755 crore and the consolidated open order book rose 36.8% to INR1,518 crore, yet management guided only low double-digit FY27 revenue growth, citing raw-material price spikes that slowed enquiry-to-order conversion and PSU-linked capex delays.

segments.name: Gear division
segments.commentary: Revenue INR416 crore (~80% of consolidated), up 16.3% YoY; order intake INR570 crore (+18.8%); open order book INR1,043 crore (+46.9%). EBIT INR75 crore at 17.9% margin vs FY26 full-year EBIT margin of 18.8%; mix 54% catalogue / 46% engineered.

segments.name: MHE division
segments.commentary: Revenue INR105 crore (-2.9% YoY) on project execution delays for power-sector orders; order intake INR185 crore (+38.1%); open order book INR475 crore (+18.8%). EBIT INR27 crore at about 25.6% margin vs FY26 full-year 24.7%; secured overseas port order of about INR21 crore.

segments.name: Overseas business
segments.commentary: Revenue INR151 crore (+21.9% YoY), led by Middle East and US; overseas order intake INR194 crore (+63%), including INR21 crore from MHE; overseas open order book INR256 crore (+73%).

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue growth guided to low double-digit percentage, described as conservative given macro uncertainty; management said it could be revisited next quarter.
Consolidated EBITDA margin to be maintained at the FY26 level (about 21%).
Gear division EBITDA margin guided to about 24%; gear EBIT margin expected around 19-20% over the next year and one year after.
MHE sustainable EBITDA margin guided at 22-24% for the year.
Exports expected to grow at least double digits in FY27; Europe recovery expected to take at least two quarters.
Mid-term FY30 revenue target of INR5,000 crore described as challenging but achievable, with Gear at 70-75% and MHE at 25-30% of revenue.
Gear revenue conversion expected to improve in Q3 and Q4 as stabilised prices are accepted; Q2 to show only gradual pick-up.
capex_capacity: Previously announced capex programme of approximately INR400 crore over FY26 to FY28 stated as on track; further capex under evaluation for board approval in near future.
Assembly centres outside India (Middle East, US and others) set up for customer proximity; some sub-assemblies locally outsourced.

Defence business has dedicated manufacturing and operating vertical built over the last 3-4 years; defence orders expected to execute over 2-3 years with working capital about 15-20% higher than the gear average.
Gear manufacturing cycle is 2-3 months for catalogue products and 4-5 months for engineered products.
demand_pricing: Gear order intake drivers: power (about 27% of order intake, including a large single order flagged in Q4 FY26), steel, cement and MHE; catalogue vs engineered order mix 27% / 73% in the quarter.

Raw-material BOM cost up about 5% on average (steel 5-7%, bearings 6-7%, fabricated gear cases about 7%, tooling 6-10%); most Q1 orders accepted with price increases and raw materials locked back-to-back on order acceptance.
Management attributed slower conversion to a sharp raw-material price increase that lengthened enquiry-to-order cycles, and to competitors holding low-cost inventory that pressured quotes.

MHE margin decline attributed to about 2.5-3% from input costs, about 3% from sales mix, and about 3% from lower throughput; MHE delays linked to design-engineering clearances on two large power-sector orders routed through EPC contractors.
Middle East growth came from orders on hold in Q4 FY26 that resumed dispatch; Middle East weakness mainly in cement and mining and minerals; Europe weak.
Sugar outlook muted due to prolonged monsoon; defence orders showed no significant update in the last 90 days; aerospace certification not being pursued.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the MHE margin fall is mix versus input costs, and what is sustainable MHE margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Management split the decline into about 2.5-3% input costs, about 3% sales mix and about 3% lower volume; sustainable MHE EBITDA margin guided at 22-24%.

qa_highlights.question: Why is gear revenue growth lagging order book growth and why only low double-digit guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Raw-material spikes slowed enquiry-to-order conversion; about INR70 crore of finished goods could not be recognised as sales in Q1 because title transfer criteria were not met by 30 June; Q2 expected only gradual pick-up, with Q3-Q4 stronger.

qa_highlights.question: Can gear costs be passed on given the small share of gear in customer capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said PSU-linked demand (thermal power, cement, steel) is sensitive to budgets; Q1 was a correction phase in pricing, with Q2 expected to be an acceptance phase. About INR160 crore of the gear order book extends beyond FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for gear standalone margins and does the business return to mid-20s?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided gear EBITDA to about 24% and gear EBIT around 19-20% over the next year and one year beyond, versus 18.8% EBIT in FY26.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY30 aspiration and segment split?
qa_highlights.answer: The INR5,000 crore FY30 revenue target was reiterated as challenging but achievable, with Gear at 70-75% and MHE at 25-30% of revenue; Gear includes marine.

qa_highlights.question: What is the working capital impact of defence orders?
qa_highlights.answer: Defence orders over 2-3 years carry higher working capital days, about 15-20% above the gear average in past similar orders, which management said would be absorbed by higher margins.

505700|2026-09.headline: Elecon Q2 FY27 revenue rose 10.5% YoY to INR639 crore and EBITDA margin expanded to 23.1%; FY27 guided to mid-double-digit growth.

Gear revenue rose 10.6% to INR488 crore, led by 30.3% overseas growth, while MHE revenue rose 10.4% to INR151 crore with MHE EBIT margin about 20.2% in Q2. Management attributed domestic softness to monsoon-related project slowness, steel price volatility and delayed project clearances, and said orders are firm and dispatch should pick up after Diwali. Management guided to medium double-digit consolidated revenue growth for H2 FY27 (around 15%) with minimum EBITDA margin at FY26 level.

qa_highlights.question: How will margins trend in H2 given commodity inflation and product mix?

qa_highlights.question: Why did MHE margin fall from about 27% to about 22%, and what happened to the power sector projects?

qa_highlights.question: What drove the Gear margin improvement?

505714|2026-06.headline: Gabriel India Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 15.5% YoY to INR1,426 crore, while EBITDA grew only 2% to INR124 crore; Project Jupiter approved.
505714|2026-06.overview: Board approved Project Jupiter: a 28.99% stake in HL Mando Anand (INR2,231 crore, of which INR1,881 crore via share allotment and INR350 crore cash) and a 30% minus 1 share stake in HL Klemove India (USD 98.44 million) as a JV in ADAS. Smaller cars grew faster than market.
Standalone revenue grew 19% YoY on healthy core suspension demand, aftermarket growth and Anchemco contribution from the restructuring.
Standalone margin pressure from commodity-driven material cost inflation; recoveries from customers lag, with some settled and others still under discussion.

505714|2026-09.headline: Gabriel India consolidated Q2 FY27 revenue rose 23% YoY to INR1,608 crore, with EBITDA up 12% to INR141 crore at an 8.8% margin.
505714|2026-09.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 23% YoY to INR1,608 crore in Q2 FY27 and EBITDA rose 12% to INR141 crore (8.8% margin), with H1 revenue up 19% to INR3,034 crore. Standalone revenue grew 23% to INR1,399 crore but standalone PBT before exceptionals rose only 7% to INR89 crore, with margin pressure from commodity, logistics and forex issues. The quarter included a new seating JV with FORVIA (signed 6 Oct 2026, incorporated 19 Oct 2026, Gabriel 50% less one share) and a partial quarter of HL Mando Anand, which closed on 11 Sep 2026. Management declared an interim dividend of INR2.15 per share and said capex will run at INR1,000-1,500 crore a year on a consolidated basis.

segments.name: Standalone suspension (PV, CV, 2W, 3W)
segments.commentary: Standalone growth was supported by core suspension demand. Management said CV growth matched the industry because Gabriel holds more than 85% share. PV lagged the market in Q2 due to a mix issue, with smaller cars growing faster and Gabriel's models underperforming.

segments.name: Fluid business (Anchemco, restructured into standalone)
segments.commentary: Anchemco was added to standalone after restructuring and contributed to revenue growth. Management said urea-linked raw material costs rose again in Q2, so price recovery from customers lagged.

segments.name: Sunroof
segments.commentary: Q2 was hit by a fire at a Hyundai supplier that disrupted Hyundai/Kia volumes. The BAYON launch began, with panoramic roofs expected to be 75-80% of its business and about 100,000 cars a year (60% India, 40% exports).

segments.name: Equity-accounted JVs/associates (Dana Anand, Henkel Anand, SK Enmove Gabriel, HL Mando Anand, HL Klemove)
segments.commentary: Share of PBT was INR48 crore in Q2 and INR91 crore in H1. HL Mando Anand and HL Klemove contributed only a few days in Q2 and will reflect fully from Q3. Management said Henkel's PAT margin was pressured by commodity and logistics costs, while Dana was offset by export forex gains.

guidance_outlook: Consolidated capex expected to run at INR1,000-1,500 crore a year.

FORVIA seating JV closing targeted by December 2026 end. The business to be transferred is the frame business, about INR150 crore in size (against a stated INR250 crore run-rate at 10% margin for the total Faurecia India seating business), with mechanisms excluded.
HL Mando Anand and HL Klemove to reflect on a full-quarter basis from Q3 FY27.
Management reaffirmed the INR50,000 crore Vision 2030 group revenue target and said the 2026 industry growth has brought it closer to that target.
Management expects Creta to phase out in FY28 with only the Creta EV continuing. AI4 SOP is expected next year, and bids are pending with Tata and Mahindra.
Management expects HL Klemove ROCE, currently below 10%, to trend toward the company average at steady state.
capex_capacity: Consolidated capex guided at INR1,000-1,500 crore a year, covering capacity, a new plant and plant improvements.
New seating JV plant to be set up, with Chennai as the planned location and Pune also cited.
Sunroof Phase 1 is operating. BC4i and BC4T are in commercial production, and AI4 is due next year. Capacity expansion for new wins depends on customer and could be capex or relocation.
Anchemco's contribution is small relative to the group, per management.
demand_pricing: Industry (Q2 FY27 production growth): 2W +16.5%, PV +25%, CV +34%, 3W +24%. H1 growth: 2W +19.5%, PV +21%, CV +25%, 3W +30.5%.
Standalone PV shock absorber share declined in H1 because Gabriel's models in the small-car segment did not keep pace with the market.
Commodity and logistics costs have squeezed price-cost recovery across subsidiaries. Management said Anchemco's urea-linked costs rose again in Q2.
2W EV: Gabriel started supplies to Bajaj Chetak in Oct 2026, and management said the order book is strong.
Seating JV product value is expected at INR30,000-50,000 per passenger car set, with mechanisms about 15-20% of seat value.
Sunroof: AYI did not ramp as expected. Hyundai fire-related disruption affected Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Which growth route (organic, new JVs, acquisitions, product expansion) will matter most toward the INR50,000 crore Vision 2030 target, and what return thresholds apply?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to the HL Klemove and FORVIA seating JVs as key steps and said ADAS and seating are high-value product areas. It did not give numbers or formal return thresholds, but said it does not compromise on ROI.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Henkel's PAT margin volatile and is it seasonal?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is not seasonal. Commodity and logistics costs have outpaced customer price recovery across businesses. Dana is offset by export forex gains.

qa_highlights.question: What is the seating JV scope, and how much of content per vehicle sits outside it?
qa_highlights.answer: The JV will be the single point of contact for the full seating system. Mechanisms, about 15-20% of seat content, will be bought from FORVIA's 100%-owned Indian mechanism company. FORVIA's seating business in India moves into the JV except mechanisms.

qa_highlights.question: Is there an anchor order for the seating JV and is a royalty payable?
qa_highlights.answer: The JV takes over existing won business, including a Volkswagen program. Value will be disclosed after closing. A royalty will be paid for technology from the Indian R&D centre, which management called normal for such deals.

qa_highlights.question: Why did PV shock absorber and CV revenue growth trail the market?
qa_highlights.answer: Atul Jaggi said CV growth matched the market given more than 85% share, with aftermarket and railway lumped into CV numbers. PV lagged mainly because of mix, with small-car models underperforming.

qa_highlights.question: What is the sunroof volume position, and what is the outlook for the next two years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said demand is improving versus last year. BC4i, BC4T and BAYON are ramping, AI4 comes next year, and Creta phases out in FY28 except for the EV version. Bids are pending with Tata and Mahindra.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue and margin perimeter for the Faurecia seating business transfer?
qa_highlights.answer: Closing is targeted for December end. The frame business, about INR150 crore in size, transfers at its current margin. Mechanisms are excluded.

qa_highlights.question: What are the growth expectations for HL Mando and HL Klemove?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects both to grow above the market. HL Mando is about 60-65% Hyundai/Kia and is adding Tata, Maruti Suzuki and Mahindra. HL Klemove is already with Hyundai, Tata and Mahindra, and is adding Maruti Suzuki.

risks_watch: Persistent commodity, logistics and forex pressure on price-cost recovery, which is visible in standalone PBT margin falling to 6.3% and in the Henkel and Anchemco margins.
PV small-car share loss, with H1 PV shock absorber share lagging the market.
Sunroof concentration on Hyundai/Kia, the Creta phase-out in FY28, and AI4 ramp timing.
Seating JV execution: closing by December 2026, plant build in Chennai and Pune, and disclosure of order book value after closing.
HL Klemove ROCE below 10% during the ramp-up phase.
Dividend and capex funding, given the INR1,000 crore NCD at 8.15%.

505726|2026-03.headline: IFB Industries Q4 FY26 revenue rose 11.0% to INR 1,456 crore and PAT to INR 33.7 crore, but FY26 commodity and forex hits of INR 84 crore were only partly offset.
505726|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue grew 11.0% YoY to INR 1,456 crore, with PBDIT margin at 5.5% against 5.3% a year earlier. PAT rose to INR 33.7 crore from INR 22.3 crore after a INR 0.58 crore Labour Code exceptional charge. For FY26, revenue grew 10% to INR 5,476 crore, while PAT rose 3.5% to INR 133.3 crore and PAT margin fell to 2.4% from 2.6%. Management said INR 67 crore of the INR 84 crore FY26 commodity and forex hit was recovered through cost initiatives and price increases. April-May commodity and forex headwinds of about INR 49 crore are only partly offset (INR 29 crore from cost initiatives so far).

qa_highlights.question: How much of the INR 84 crore commodity and forex hit was recovered, and does it reverse next year?
qa_highlights.answer: INR 67 crore was recovered in FY26 via cost initiatives and price increases. Management expects INR 120 crore more from cost initiatives over 10 months, with the P&L benefit from any commodity or forex easing.

qa_highlights.question: What is the commodity and forex hit so far in Q1 FY27?

505726|2026-09.headline: IFB Industries Q2 FY27 revenue rose 14.04% to INR1,512 crore, but PBDIT margin fell to 6.01% from 7.73% on commodity and forex pressure.
505726|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue grew 14.04% YoY to INR1,512 crore, while PBDIT fell 11.3% to INR90.92 crore and margin compressed about 172 bps to 6.01%. PAT declined to INR39.56 crore from INR49.75 crore, with management attributing the squeeze to material cost inflation from commodities and a weaker rupee. Management said price hikes have not recovered the cost increase and that the 10% appliance EBITDA margin target is no longer intact. Engineering was described as on budget, with new EV-focused capex in Gujarat and a planned chain plant, and the Sanand Tata project proceeding.

segments.name: Home Appliances

segments.name: Engineering
segments.commentary: Budget was met on top line and bottom line, with growth from fine blanking and stampings. Mix is about 50% two-wheeler, 40% four-wheeler, and 10% electrical and three-wheeler; order booking is INR220 crore against a INR500 crore target.

segments.name: Steel
segments.commentary: Furnace annealing capacity was raised from 1,500-1,700 tons to 2,800 tons per month, and management is stabilising the ramp. Sales split is about 60% internal and 40% external.

segments.commentary: Management claims about 20-25% market share and number one position; market estimated at INR400-500 crore against INR104 crore of revenue last year.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 10% EBITDA margin target for appliances still intact given commodity and forex pressure?
qa_highlights.answer: Sandeep Abraham said no. Material costs rose about 4 percentage points of net revenue and BOM rose about 4.3%; price hikes have fallen short of this.

qa_highlights.question: Why has growth slowed to 10.5% in Q2 and is 20% still the target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the Q2 slowdown to Diwali shifting into Q3 (8 November 2026 versus 20 October 2025). H1 grew about 14.5%, and 20% was called aspirational.

qa_highlights.question: Should engineering be demerged, and are there plans to consolidate plants?
qa_highlights.answer: Arup Das said there is no demerger proposal at present. Soumitra Goswami said there is no current plan to consolidate the 10 manufacturing facilities.

qa_highlights.question: What are the engineering capex, asset turnover and H2 outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex of about INR103 crore is planned for the Gujarat EV plant in two phases (FY27 and FY28). Asset turnover was not answered and management would revert.

qa_highlights.question: Is the industry taking price increases, and why are margins under pressure versus peers?
qa_highlights.answer: Sandeep Abraham said large-appliance pricing could be higher but is held back by competitiveness and a cautious industry stance in the festive period. Small appliances have a lower ticket-size sensitivity.

qa_highlights.question: Is IFB open to using debt for expansion and any acquisition updates?
qa_highlights.answer: Soumitra Goswami said the policy has been 1:1 debt to equity, with the engineering expansion under review and no decision yet. Arup Das said more than 72 companies have been evaluated for synergy and non-disruptive products.

505729|2026-03.headline: Singer India Q4 FY26 revenue rose 37% to Rs 166.3 crore and FY26 revenue reached Rs 557 crore, up 29%, led by Sewing Machines.
505729|2026-03.overview: Management reported Q4 FY26 revenue of Rs 166.3 crore (up 37%), PBT of Rs 8 crore (up 43%) and EBITDA of Rs 9.3 crore (up 49%). For FY26, revenue was Rs 557 crore (up 29%), EBITDA Rs 21.5 crore (up 70%) and PBT Rs 17.3 crore (up 73%), after a one-time labour code cost of Rs 73 lakh; adjusted EBITDA was Rs 22.2 crore and adjusted PBT Rs 18.1 crore. Sewing Machines drove growth, while Appliances revenue grew about 10% in Q4 but its segment result fell by about Rs 2 crore. Management gave no formal guidance and did not answer questions on promoter exit or M&A.

segments.name: Appliances
segments.commentary: Revenue grew about 10% in Q4 on e-commerce range and fans, but segment result was lower by about Rs 2 crore due to EPR costs and fan business build-out. Demand muted, trade inventory blocked, dealer cash flows tight.

segments.name: Fans
segments.commentary: Fan business grew about 50% in Q4 with a new range covering economy, base, decorative, BLDC, TPW and exhaust fans; supply chain constrained by labour shortage and cost inflation.

qa_highlights.answer: More than 60% of government supply is complete; the remaining 40% is expected before the start of H2 FY27. Growth came from government, retail and e-commerce.

505872|2026-09.headline: WPIL Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue fell 17% YoY to INR354 crores as domestic project and product dispatches slipped, while H1 revenue rose 6% to INR855 crores.
505872|2026-09.overview: Consolidated Q2 FY27 revenue was INR354 crores, down 17% YoY, and standalone revenue was INR118 crores, down 33% YoY. H1 consolidated revenue rose 6% to INR855 crores, EBITDA fell 5% to INR123 crores, and EBITDA margin was 14.33%. Management attributed the weakness to deferred product dispatches (monsoon-hit site acceptance), slow domestic project execution tied to unpaid West Bengal JJM funds, and lumpy South African project revenue, and guided to a stronger H2. Management did not quantify the deferred dispatches or give an FY27 revenue guidance number.

505978|2026-03.headline: Triton Valves Q4 FY26 revenue rose to about ₹159 crore (from ₹142 crore YoY), with FY26 adjusted PBT near ₹15.5 crore, roughly double the prior year.

EBITDA was eroded by simultaneous rises in copper/zinc and the US dollar, which management said it passes to customers with a one-quarter lag. Climate control remained weak due to Chinese dumping, while metals gained from a second casting line and tube/alloy orders. The NCLT order for the merger of Tritonvalves Climatech into Triton Valves was described as expected within one to two weeks.

506194|2026-03.headline: Arihant Superstructures Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 18.5% YoY to Rs 181 crore; FY26 EBITDA margin 23% and FY27 margin guided to 25-27%.

506194|2026-06.headline: Arihant Superstructures Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 9% YoY to INR 132 crore, with EBITDA margin at 21% and PAT at INR 10 crore.

Net debt stood at INR 818 crore against net worth of INR 460 crore, and management reiterated plans to reduce debt from next year while funding hotel and club assets. Management guided to 2,500 unit deliveries by FY27-end and said no new land acquisitions are planned this year.

Average project timeline is about 4 years (range 3-5 years from start to completion).

Navi Mumbai's share of the MMR market rose from 12% to 17% over three years, with Thane and Kalyan losing share.
Labour and skill shortages and higher construction costs are raising input costs; management says inventory on hand offsets this with no balance-sheet impact.

Management is holding price rather than chasing volume.

qa_highlights.question: How much cost saving is captured and what further reduction is achievable?

qa_highlights.question: Timeline for converting pre-sales into revenue, given pre-sales of INR 1,731 million vs reported revenue of INR 1,316 million?
qa_highlights.answer: Pre-sales take about 90 days on average to enter revenue recognition under percentage-of-completion, covering owner contribution, agreement, registration and NOCs.

qa_highlights.question: Are new land acquisitions attractive given higher costs?

qa_highlights.question: Where will the premium share of the project mix reach, and will geography be diversified?

qa_highlights.question: What drives average realisation, and how do margins and ROCE evolve?

506395|2026-03.headline: Coromandel Q4 FY26 revenue rose 19% to INR 6,068 crore and EBITDA 16% to INR 494 crore, but reported PAT fell to INR 115 crore on last year's land-sale gain.
506395|2026-03.overview: Q4 operations were strong: consolidated revenue grew 19% YoY to INR 6,068 crore and EBITDA rose 16% to INR 494 crore, with the fertilizer plants run full after the annual turnaround. Reported PAT of INR 115 crore compared with INR 578 crore last year, which included a INR 347 crore land-sale exceptional gain; this year carried a INR 71 crore impairment on drone-business investments and goodwill. Fertilizer margins compressed sharply as Middle East disruption spiked ammonia and sulphur prices, while crop protection, specialty nutrients, retail and NACL performed well. Management gave no quantitative guidance on fertilizer margins or subsidy outcomes, pending government support.

segments.name: Fertilizers (DAP/NPK/SSP/Nano)
segments.commentary: Record fertilizer production of 3.5 million tons and record DAP+NPK sales of 4.3 million tons (+7%), with 17.5% phosphatic market share; Q4 fertilizer manufacturing EBITDA was below INR 3,500 per ton versus over INR 5,000 per ton last year. SSP sales hit a record 8.4 lakh tons, and Nano DAP volumes grew 60% to about 42 lakh bottles.

segments.name: Crop protection (standalone)
segments.commentary: Revenue rose 15% to INR 3,054 crore and profit 55% to INR 569 crore for FY26; FY26 revenue mix was exports INR 1,450 crore, domestic B2B INR 700 crore and formulations INR 900 crore. Q4 standalone crop protection growth was about 2%, attributed to export sales being moved into Q1 and a bio export order shipped earlier.

segments.name: NACL (Nagarjuna Agrichem, 53% stake)
segments.commentary: Consolidated crop protection with NACL reached about INR 4,000 crore; NACL FY26 revenue INR 1,585 crore (+28%) and EBITDA INR 103 crore, with margin at 6-7% and guided to 9-10% next year.

segments.name: Retail
segments.commentary: Retail grew over 30% in FY26 with more than 300 new stores in Andhra Pradesh, Telangana and Karnataka, and entry into Maharashtra and Tamil Nadu.

segments.name: Dhaksha (drones, subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Impairment of INR 71 crore taken on investments and goodwill due to long lead times in order execution; management expects recovery after first large order executes this year.

guidance_outlook: Crop protection (standalone) revenue growth guided at 20-25% for the coming year, with domestic formulations growing 20-25% and six new product launches.
Sarigam active ingredient expansion of 20,000 tons is due around mid-2026 with payback under two years; Dahej Mancozeb debottlenecking of 10,000 tons has payback under one year.
Granulation capacity expansion expected to commission by December 2026.
Rock phosphate output in Senegal to rise 30-40% in FY27 from more than 3.5 lakh tons in FY26.
Trading margin of roughly 4-5% per ton; trading volumes may fall in Q1 FY27 on DAP availability, with second-half recovery expected.
Management declined to give fertilizer EBITDA per ton or margin guidance for FY27, citing fluid conditions and pending subsidy compensation.
Raw material cover secured for Q1 FY27; Q2 cover depends on Middle East resolution. Sulphur visibility is up to June.
capex_capacity: Kakinada: 2,000 tpd sulphuric acid and 650 tpd phosphoric acid plant commissioned in March 2026 (about 200,000 tons per year phosphoric acid); in trial runs, with stable operations expected from April-May 2026.
Dahej: technical plant commissioned in FY26 and Mancozeb capacity expanded by 10,000 tons; Sarigam expansion of 20,000 tons under way.
Technical MAP plant and seaweed granulation capacity under development.
Fluorination chemistry investment planned for CDMO opportunity; small-scale capacity to be created this year, production next year.
Coromandel has invested over INR 3,000 crore across segments in the last two years.
Coromandel's stake in the Senegal mining company increased to 71.5%.
demand_pricing: Industry: IMD forecasts below-normal monsoon for kharif 2026, though key southern markets are likely to see normal rainfall; updated IMD forecast due in late May.
NBS rates for kharif 2026 raised about 10% for N, P and S, which management said do not reflect the sharp rise in raw material prices and rupee depreciation.
Ammonia and sulphur are trading around USD 840-850 and USD 800 per ton respectively; phosphoric acid price for the quarter fixed at USD 1,360 versus USD 1,290 previously.
Q4 rupee range of 89.75-95.23 per USD; management said depreciation helps the crop protection export business.
Crop protection raw materials said to be covered, with input cost increases passed through; Mancozeb cost increases passed through to customers.
Rabi season demand was muted due to late monsoon withdrawal, with lower-than-expected liquidation.
Unique grades remained at about 35% of fertilizer sales on an annualized basis.

qa_highlights.question: Why is there a gap between consolidated and standalone P&L, and how will BMCC's depreciation and profitability evolve?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said BMCC (mining) has turned profitable on better volumes and fixed-cost absorption, and the gap is mainly consolidation amortization of acquisition-related intangibles, not operating loss.

qa_highlights.question: How will fertilizer margins hold up given only about a 10% NBS increase against sharp raw material inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is seeking additional subsidy and cost-to-cost reimbursement for June-September, with discussions at an early stage; it declined to quantify the amount. Any remaining gap may be passed on through MRP corrections, and industry has already made some MRP corrections in the last one to two months.

qa_highlights.question: What are the crop protection growth, margin and NACL margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Standalone crop protection targets 20-25% revenue growth with margins sustained near 19%; NACL margin improved to 6-7%, can reach 9-10% next year, and restoring 7-8% needs no major investment.

qa_highlights.question: What is the full-year split of subsidy versus non-subsidy EBITDA and of crop protection revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Subsidy share of EBITDA was 57% in Q4 and 66% for FY26. Standalone FY26 crop protection revenue was exports INR 1,450 crore, domestic B2B INR 700 crore and formulations INR 900 crore; NACL FY26 revenue was INR 1,584 crore and Q4 INR 361 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What is the fertilizer finished goods inventory and trading exposure?
qa_highlights.answer: Finished fertilizer inventory is about 5.5 lakh tons, of which trading is about 60,000-70,000 tons. Trading margin is roughly 4-5%, and FY27 trading volume may fall in Q1 because of DAP import shortages.

qa_highlights.question: Why was standalone crop protection growth only about 2% in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q4 is off-season, export sales were deliberately moderated to shift into April-May, and a bio export order was executed earlier in December; full-year crop protection growth was 16%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the sulphur and ammonia sourcing position, and is Q2 covered?
qa_highlights.answer: Sulphur has visibility up to June, with diversified spot sourcing from Canada, South Asia and Japan; ammonia and sulphur prices are about USD 800-850 per ton. Management said Q2 coverage depends on Strait of Hormuz shipping and a Middle East resolution.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for Dhaksha, the drone subsidiary?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said technical gaps are fixed and a large order is awaiting execution, with the first order this year expected to build confidence; a larger facility is due around May 2026.

506395|2026-06.headline: Coromandel Q1 FY27 consolidated EBITDA fell 3% YoY to INR761 crores on West Asia input-cost spike, while revenue rose 15% to INR8,215 crores.
506395|2026-06.overview: Consolidated total income rose 15% YoY to INR8,215 crores, helped by higher fertilizer realisations and non-subsidy growth, with NACL now consolidated. EBITDA declined 3% to INR761 crores and net profit fell to INR382 crores from INR502 crores as ammonia and sulphur costs outran NBS subsidy rates. Management said phosphate production was deliberately cut to 6.9 lakh tons (72% utilisation) to protect inventory economics, while Crop Protection (revenue +20%, EBIT +44%) and Retail (revenue +85%) carried the quarter. Management is pressing the government for a kharif NBS revision and says no near-term fertilizer capacity additions are planned.

segments.name: Fertilizers (phosphatic)

segments.name: Specialty nutrients and organics
segments.commentary: Described as strong, aided by higher organics and micronutrient offtake; launched 3 new products. Management says this business grows 25-30% with about 20% EBITDA margin.

segments.name: Crop Protection
segments.commentary: Record Q1: revenue +20% to INR870 crores, EBIT +44% to INR159 crores, with exports and B2B strong. New products are 32% of domestic B2C sales vs 23% last year.

segments.name: Retail
segments.commentary: Revenue +85% YoY; 76% of stores profitable vs 61% last year; 22 new stores take network above 1,200 outlets.

segments.name: Nano and bio products
segments.commentary: Nano business volumes +2% YoY with nearly 60% market share; UP and Maharashtra bans are restraining growth. Bio business steady, with 2 new products launched.

guidance_outlook: Phosphoric acid price for Q2 settled at $1,700/t vs $1,360/t in Q1, following higher DAP and raw-material prices.
Granulation project on track for commissioning in Q4 FY27; Crop Protection capacity expansion for key molecules expected by September 2026.

Management wants kharif NBS rates revised to the 6-month average policy formula; says the industry has taken a 25-30% price increase across grades, and that further price rises are not feasible without subsidy correction.
Sulphur expected to stay high for some time; management says the acid-backed production economics are unattractive until sulphur falls, with NACL-type steady-state EBITDA well below Coromandel.

Granulation project on track for Q4 FY27 commissioning; new capacity is 750,000 tonnes, 50% to be sold via own retail and the balance into UP, Rajasthan, MP and Chhattisgarh.

Kakinada T-MAP plant and seaweed granulation plant progressing; Ankleshwar fluorination launch facility being set up; IIT Chennai research park planned; PA-SA plant gives about 60% acid self-sufficiency.
demand_pricing: Monsoon deficit was 23% through the quarter, moderating to 17% by late July; reservoirs at 34% of capacity vs 57% last year. Pulses acreage down 15%, oilseeds and cotton down 6%, and paddy back to normal.
Management says there is no fertilizer shortage; Urea and DAP stocks are comfortable for kharif, but industry production and imports must hold for two more months to build rabi carryover.
NP/NPK production and imports fell 21% and 38% respectively; management ties this to weak NBS subsidy for these grades.

NACL export revenue hit by price moderation on molecules sold to global MNCs, while Coromandel passed input-cost increases through to exports.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a structural shift to NPK or a fertilizer shortage on the ground?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no shortage; the early-season pick-up of low-MRP packs was an advance purchase, and current uptake depends more on monsoon than on availability.

qa_highlights.question: How much did FX contribute to Crop Protection EBITDA?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FX is at most 5-6% of consolidated EBITDA, under a netting-based hedging policy.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the depreciation spike and how much is from new capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Incremental depreciation from new capex is about INR16-18 crores; the rest is mining overburden amortisation (about INR30 crores) and NACL intangibles amortisation (about INR20-21 crores).

qa_highlights.question: What is the ask from government and how is the EBITDA per ton outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management wants the 6-month average NBS rate applied, and says NP/NPK rates need significant correction; the target is nutrient EBITDA of about INR6,500/t from INR5,000/t, but not in the current quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex plan for the next 1-2 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided normal sustainable capex of about INR300 crores, but will consider higher spending for attractive-return projects.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Dhaksha drone contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Coromandel bought 100-150 drones this quarter and targets a fleet of 500 during the year; management said Dhaksha is not a significant EBITDA drag.

506395|2026-09.headline: Coromandel Q2 FY27: EBITDA fell 18% to ₹944 crore on NPK margin compression, while revenue rose 6% to ₹10,348 crore.
506395|2026-09.overview: Q2 was hit by deficient monsoon rainfall in key states, a roughly 40% industry-wide fall in NPK production and consumption, high raw material (sulphur, ammonia) costs and thin NBS rates. Coromandel cut primary sales about 30% and production 15% to 7.7 lakh tonnes to manage working capital, while lifting its market share from 17% to 19%. Crop protection revenue rose 22%, but NACL's EBITDA fell sharply on high-cost carryover inventory. Management said the new NBS rates for the Rabi 2026-27 season were approved the previous day and should support MRP correction and NPK volume recovery, though it is still awaiting the detailed notification.

segments.name: Nutrients (NPK / DAP / SSP)
segments.commentary: Primary sales fell about 30% and consumption about 33%, with production cut 15% to 7.7 lakh tonnes. Market share rose from 17% to 19%. SSP volumes fell 13% to 1.9 lakh tonnes.

segments.name: Crop protection
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 22%, driven by export markets, which were about 45% of revenue. Domestic demand stayed soft, and six new products were launched across agrochemicals and biologics.

segments.name: NACL (subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Revenue was ₹374 crore, down 18%, and EBITDA was ₹12 crore, sharply lower on carryover high-cost inventory and falling prices for certain molecules.

segments.name: Retail
segments.commentary: Network grew by 80 stores in Q2 to 1,300 stores across five states, with a target of 2,000 in two years. Retail white-label brands are expected to cross ₹100 crore annual sales this year.

segments.name: Non-subsidy businesses (retail, specialty nutrients, bio, SSP)
segments.commentary: Management said these grew strongly and drove EBITDA despite the NACL drag, although non-subsidy sales in UP and Maharashtra were hit by state bans on non-substitutable fertilisers.

guidance_outlook: Management expects Rabi MRP corrections of at least 10-15% for NP/NPK grades, subject to the detailed NBS notification and the subsidy offsetting negative margins.
Backward-integration (phosphoric acid) spread is expected to improve in H2 as the Kakinada plant returns to full capacity from October; management called ~$350/t a safe assumption.
Grassroots granulation plant in Kakinada is targeted for commissioning by February 2027, with the capacity usable in the next season.
Management expects consumption and channel inventory to normalise by year-end, with NPK share recovering toward the historical mix.
Sulphur prices are expected to soften toward $900/t, with a possibility of falling below $500/t if purchases stay smart; DAP was rolled over at $700/t, and phosphoric acid prices held at $1,700/t.
Management said it is cautiously optimistic about Rabi, but expects some time before NACL's margins recover.
capex_capacity: Kakinada sulphuric acid and phosphoric acid plant was commissioned in Q2 and ran at reduced rates until sulphur supply resumed in August; it is now operating at full capacity.
Greenfield granulation plant in Kakinada is due for commissioning by February 2027, with ~₹2,000 crore invested in the phosphoric acid plant.
A flow-chemistry launch plant is being set up, with a possible commercial plant costing ₹200-300 crore in 1-2 years, subject to customer sign-ups.
A capacity expansion of one key agrochemical molecule was announced, planned for this month.
Mining operations at Senegal are being scaled up, and management said it will not go to 100% captive raw material supply.
demand_pricing: Industry-wide NPK production and consumption fell about 40% in Q2 as the DAP-NPK price gap pushed farmers toward DAP.
Industry NPK sales for H1 were about 60 lakh tonnes vs 121 lakh tonnes last year (management's figures); DAP was about 44 lakh tonnes.
Management said the DAP-NPK mix moved from about 60:40 to 30:70, and expects it to normalise with the new NBS rates.
Channel inventory is estimated at 5-7% above last year, and management expects it to fall by year-end.
Nano DAP is the market leader, with growing exports and registrations under way in Latin America, the Middle East and South Asia, but state bans have constrained sales.

506405|2026-09.headline: Q2 FY27 revenue about Rs. 273 crore but EBITDA fell to Rs. 11.6 crore as sulfur spike caused sulfuric acid demand destruction and plants ran at about 65%.

Pass-through of higher sulfur costs worked in Q1 but not in Q2, as end markets such as fertilizer and detergents cut demand. Management also deliberately ran the acid plant at low utilisation (about 65% of a 100 capacity, with the acid plant run only to supply specialty plants) and said the Q1 inventory gain did not repeat. Management said specialty chemicals traction, including new overseas markets, was obscured by the commodity result, and that sulfur prices are now easing.

506590|2026-06.headline: PCBL Q1 FY27: consolidated revenue up 17% to INR2,474 crore, EBITDA up 23% to INR400 crore, PAT up 65% to INR155 crore, helped by low-cost inventory gains.
506590|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue rose 17% YoY to INR2,474 crore and EBITDA rose 23% to INR400 crore, with PAT up 65% to INR155 crore. Management attributed part of the margin to spot-market pricing during the crude spike (Brent averaged USD 97/bbl vs USD 78 in Q4 FY26) and to low-cost inventory, which it said will partly reverse. Carbon black volumes were flat at 153,513 tonnes as export volumes were diverted to higher-margin domestic spot, and management guided Q2 volumes lower on customer destocking before a recovery in H2. Aquapharm (new CEO Rohit Narang) delivered revenue of INR394 crore and EBITDA of INR47 crore, with oil and gas weak YoY.

financial_highlights.change: reduced as volume diverted to domestic spot
INR40-50 crore expected to reverse next quarter

Europe carbon black volume about 16,000 MT and US about 4,800 MT in Q1.

US customers diversifying away from China and Russia; management says PCBL is more competitive in the US than pre-conflict despite higher freight.
Aquapharm: phosphonates growing in Asia; Europe shifting to green chelates; oil and gas demand volatile with customer inventory overhang in the Americas.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the quarter's profit came from low-cost inventory gains, and how much of the performance chemicals volume dip is export-linked?
qa_highlights.answer: Low-cost inventory benefit was about INR70 crore in Q1, of which INR40-50 crore may reverse next quarter. Performance chemicals volume was diverted to domestic market because export margins were lower on higher freight; specialty is about 70% international and was not hit.

qa_highlights.question: What is the tariff refund amount and where will it be booked?
qa_highlights.answer: Combined refund for Aquapharm and PCBL is about INR40-45 crore; application is filed and receipt expected in 2-4 weeks. Accounting treatment (top line vs other income) to be confirmed with auditors.

qa_highlights.question: What is the sustainable Aquapharm EBITDA per tonne and full-year run rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 EBITDA/tonne about INR20,000 vs about INR19,500 a year ago. Next quarter may be lower due to inventory adjustment; management expects full-year EBITDA/tonne to be sustainable at similar levels. Utilisation remains low.

qa_highlights.question: Why did carbon black volumes fall QoQ and YoY despite the Chennai line, and what is the gross profit per kg trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it chose not to deliver some international orders where logistics ate margins, and held low-cost inventory for sale when new prices came in. Destocking in Q2; volume recovery expected in Q3 and Q4. Gross profit per tonne targeted at about INR36-38 for the remaining nine months, a trade-off with volume.

qa_highlights.question: What are the Q1 carbon black EBITDA per tonne, FY27 guidance and capex outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 carbon black EBITDA was about INR22,900/MT. FY27 guidance of 14-15% above FY26 average, about INR16,500-17,000/MT, reiterated. FY27 capex about INR300 crore (plus or minus INR50 crore), with strategic capex up to about INR100 crore; Andhra greenfield spend mainly in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of Nanovace and the long-term INR1,000 crore EBITDA ambition?
qa_highlights.answer: Pilot plant is up, with machine-level trials done and line balancing ongoing; first batch to customers expected in the next few weeks, with sampling in August. Management reiterated that Nanovace will hit its targets, without restating timelines or the INR1,000 crore figure.

Aquapharm: oil and gas volatility with inventory overhang in the Americas; exit run-rate of INR75 crore EBITDA not reaffirmed by the new CEO; raw material availability and LPG constraints.
Spot-price exposure: about one-third of volumes on spot, with part of the margin tied to crude moves that may moderate.
Cost programme: INR200-250 crore savings over 4-6 quarters, with delivery in reported results still to be shown; coal tar distillation capex approvals expected within about a month.
key_quotes: Close to a third of our volumes are on the spot market, and our teams monetize this exposure very effectively as crude ran up sharply through April and May, capturing strong realizations.
We see this as a timing effect, not a demand effect and therefore, remain constructive on the second half of FY27.
This quarter we have some extraordinary benefit of low-cost inventory, which is unlikely to be repeated in subsequent quarters.
So Nanovace, we continue to hold that it will hit the targets that we had set ourselves.

506590|2026-09.headline: PCBL Q2 FY27 revenue rose 14% YoY to INR 2,474 crores and PAT 20% to INR 74 crores, despite carbon black volumes of 134,180 tonnes.
506590|2026-09.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 14% YoY to INR 2,474 crores, EBITDA rose 12% to INR 310 crores and PAT grew 20% to INR 74 crores, on pricing discipline and cost actions. Carbon black volumes were weak as management let go of low-margin spot and Southeast Asian orders, and the company said it would not chase volume. Management kept the EBITDA-per-tonne guidance but flagged that the volume growth target of about 7% is now challenging. Crude moved back above $100 during the quarter, which lifted realisations, and Russian CBFS supply disruption is expected to keep feedstock tight.

financial_highlights.change: Exports down 18% QoQ per analyst question; no YoY figure stated

financial_highlights.value: About INR 19,800 (INR 17,500 excluding about INR 2,300 tariff refund)
186 million units, of which 108 million units sold externally at INR 5.34 per unit

segments.name: Carbon black (consolidated)
segments.commentary: Volume of 134,180 tonnes split into tyre grades 77,914 t, performance chemicals 39,698 t and specialty grades 16,568 t. Volume fell as spot business in Southeast Asia and domestic spot was let go on margin grounds.

segments.name: Power
segments.commentary: 186 million units generated, 108 million units sold externally at INR 5.34/unit. Output was lower as Southeast Asia production was cut, and about 40% of power is used captively.

segments.name: Aquapharm
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 433 crores and EBITDA INR 42 crores on 24,253 MT. Home Care volume rose 7% YoY, Water Solutions and Oil & Gas each fell 20% YoY, and application-specific solutions grew 15%.

guidance_outlook: Reiterated double-digit growth in average EBITDA per tonne over FY26 levels.
Financial (EBITDA) guidance unchanged; volume growth of about 7% for FY27 described as challenging, so volume may come in below the initial plan.
Aquapharm targets double-digit revenue growth for FY27 and for H2 FY27, with new products (PBTC, GLDA, Green Chelates) as volume drivers.
Management expects a strong H2 but says the timing of recovery depends on market conditions; buying patterns expected to improve gradually.
INR 200-250 crore cost-saving programme (Project Alchemy) still targeted, with INR 10-15 crores captured so far; acceleration expected from coming quarters.
Coal distillation (backward integration) capex, part of INR 300 crore FY27 capex plan, is in final approval; announcement expected shortly.
Antidumping duty on HEDP and ATMP is provisional; not included in Aquapharm forecasts.
capex_capacity: Specialty carbon black capacity about 75 kt; Mundra Line 6 already commercialised and volumes can be dialled up as gas and feedstock become available.
Andhra capacity addition; total potential output of about 8 lakh tonnes including Andhra, about 2 lakh tonnes above current volumes, with a significant share intended for exports.
Super Conductive Black facility commissioned; Acetylene Black on track under the ECMS framework.
Nanovace (51% JV with Kinaltek) pilot at Palej producing samples now in internal qualification; silicon carbon composite development across Palej, Belgium and Australia.
US railcar infrastructure and Antwerp warehouse being set up to support export volumes.
Management said it may slightly postpone some capex decisions if needed.
demand_pricing: Crude moved back to about $110 (from about $70 at Q1 time), so there was no inventory give-back; only about INR 10-15 crores of Q1 inventory gain passed to customers early in Q2.
Price increase announced in the spot market, with further increases expected in November and December.
Russian refinery throughput at multi-decade lows, keeping global CBFS tight; Chinese coal tar prices firmed, supporting SE Asia prices.
Russian and Chinese imports into India declining over recent months as Russian supply tightened and Chinese coal tar costs rose.
Customers destocked in Q2; some tyre customers who stocked up in Q1 are expected to return volume in Q3.

Feedstock: about 80-85% previously sourced from the Gulf; US mix unchanged, with diversification to multiple US vendors and sourcing from Southeast Asia under negotiation, with a possible 1-2% premium on that volume.
Competition: some players are chasing volume at low prices in the domestic market, per management; management says this is unsustainable.
Europe market growth expected at about 1-2% next year; US tariff volatility still restraining large customers from shifting volumes.

qa_highlights.question: How did inventory and pass-through of higher China coal tar prices play out in Q2, and what happens in Q3?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said crude stayed elevated rather than falling back, so there was no inventory give-back, with only about INR 10-15 crores of Q1 gains passed through early in Q2. Spot price increases are in place and further increases are expected in November and December.

qa_highlights.question: Why did power revenue fall, and what drives power generation?
qa_highlights.answer: Aquapharm incurred about INR 10 crores of higher power purchase cost. Generation fell because Southeast Asia volumes were cut, and it should rise as production scales up this quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Cost reduction quantification and outlook under the INR 200-250 crore programme?
qa_highlights.answer: Most of the fixed cost decline was volume-driven, with about INR 10-15 crores from Project Alchemy so far. Management expects acceleration as initiatives are standardised over the coming months.

qa_highlights.question: Export volume outlook for FY27 and the likely contribution from new capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects a return to international growth as coal tar prices rise, with US railcar infrastructure unlocking volume. It expects significant export growth over the next few years through long-term tie-ups.

qa_highlights.question: Volume guidance after a weak Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: The EBITDA guidance is unchanged, but the roughly 7% volume growth target is now challenging on raw material availability and competition. Volume may be lower than the initial plan, with spot opportunities in Q3 and Q4 to be pursued.

qa_highlights.question: Carbon black spread for the quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR 19,800 per tonne EBITDA, of which about INR 2,300 was the US tariff refund, giving roughly INR 17,500 per tonne excluding the refund.

risks_watch: Crude price volatility (around $70 to $110 range in the period) affecting customer destocking and buying patterns.
Russian CBFS shortfall and Chinese coal tar price moves, which drive feedstock cost and spread.
Freight and war-risk premiums on feedstock and exports, with some export business unprofitable without pass-through freight.
Volume target risk: about 7% FY27 volume growth now seen as challenging.
Antidumping duty on HEDP and ATMP still provisional and unquantified.
Aquapharm H2 seasonality (Q3 dip) and US oil and gas investment hesitancy.
US tariff volatility holding back large export customers.

And we are not chasing volumes. We would rather keep this capacity spare.
We reiterate our guidance of double-digit growth in average EBITDA per tonne over FY26 levels.

rows.why: Spot price increase already announced with further rises expected in November and December, supported by Russian CBFS supply tightness and firming Chinese coal tar prices.
