rows.why: Customers destocked in Q2 and some tyre customers who stocked up in Q1 are expected to return volume in Q3, though management tied the recovery timing to market conditions.

506618|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 8.7% YoY to INR347.2 crores, with EBITDA up 18.8% to INR40.8 crores at an 11.8% margin.
506618|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations was INR347.2 crores, up 8.7% YoY from INR319.5 crores, with gross margin at 36.6% (up 355 bps) and EBITDA of INR40.8 crores (11.8% margin). PAT was INR22.1 crores, up 7% YoY, a 6.4% margin. Management said Indian agrochemical demand is weak from delayed sowing and a weak monsoon, with pricing pressure in India and adverse European weather delaying buying. Q1 growth was driven by exports (up 27.7%) on better inventory planning, while domestic revenue fell 3.1%. Management reiterated its guidance of 15-20% revenue growth for FY27 and a 15% EBITDA margin over 2-3 years, with H2 expected to be stronger.

segments.commentary: Supplies leading global beverage companies in India, with more customers added over the last two quarters. Segment margin is targeted to improve over 2-3 years.

EBITDA margin is expected to improve gradually through the year; 15% EBITDA margin target is maintained over the next 2-3 years.
New products targeted at 15-18% of FY27 revenue, rising above 20% next year.

Two MoU products expected to ramp from Q4 FY27 after customer approval; two herbicide intermediates to launch this year, each contributing about INR10-20 crores in year one and INR40-50 crores at peak in 2-4 years.

Management reports customers in Europe and Japan and in India are seeking China-plus-one sourcing from India, but Japanese conversions take longer.
Top 5 customers contribute 60-65% of revenue and top 10 about 75%.

506618|2026-09.headline: Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 28% YoY to INR326.7 crore, but gross margin fell to 34.1% and PAT to INR13.5 crore (4.1% margin).
506618|2026-09.overview: Revenue grew 28% YoY on domestic growth of 60%, while exports were flat at about 1.3%. Gross margin compressed about 540 bps to 34.1% from raw material inflation and new-product learning-curve effects. EBITDA rose 12.6% to INR29.6 crore at a 9% margin. H1 PAT fell 9.3% to INR35.5 crore because about INR9 crore of prior-year other income (FX gains and tax-refund interest) did not recur. Management said deferred export orders should flow into Q3 and Q4.

segments.name: Exports

segments.name: Segment reporting

H1 FY27 capex about INR28 crore, of which incremental gross block was about INR16 crore; the rest was capital advances. Management said the spend is asset renewal, as assets are about 40 years old.

qa_highlights.question: Why did margins fall despite higher new-product share (19% in Q2)?

qa_highlights.answer: Management said the spend is asset renewal on assets about 40 years old, and that a greenfield project is at an advanced stage with shortlisted plots.

qa_highlights.question: Funding mix and debt needs for the INR100 crore capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Funding is about 25% equity and 75% debt. Equity will come from internal accruals, and additional debt sanction is already in place, to be drawn as the project progresses.

qa_highlights.question: Why did trade receivables jump from INR203.5 crore in FY26 to over INR450 crore at September 2026?
qa_highlights.answer: Extended credit terms were granted to major international customers because of geopolitical conditions. Management expects receivables to fall in Q3 and Q4 and reach a normal range by year-end.

qa_highlights.question: What revenue can the MoU products contribute in FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Each product was guided at INR30-50 crore a year. Due to long overseas approval cycles (Japan, Europe), FY28 is expected to be INR15-20 crore, with gradual ramp-up over two years.

506655|2026-03.headline: Sudarshan Q4 FY26 reported EBITDA INR73 crore, business EBITDA INR118 crore; net debt cut to INR755 crore from INR934 crore in Dec-25.
506655|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 showed a sharp sequential recovery as insolvency-era customer destocking ended and volumes returned, with the acquired Heubach/Clariant pigments group delivering EUR11 million business EBITDA versus a EUR9-10 million plan. Inventory was cut by EUR29 million against a EUR20 million plan, which released INR82 crore of overhead from the balance sheet and lifted P&L EBITDA. Reported EBITDA of INR73 crore included a one-time non-cash PPA credit of INR37 crore, and depreciation fell to about INR50 crore for the quarter after the final purchase price allocation. Management guided to EUR35 million EBITDA for FY27 and reiterated EUR90-100 million over three to four years, while flagging Middle East-driven raw material, energy and logistics pressure.

segments.commentary: FY26 revenue was flattish, hit by distributor rationalisation in Europe and LatAm; integration costs slightly dented EBITDA. Management guides 8-10% growth for FY27 and expects to keep healthy margins.

segments.name: Acquired group (Heubach/Clariant pigments)
segments.commentary: Q4 business EBITDA EUR11 million, with FY26 EBITDA turning positive on value capture. Management guides EUR35 million EBITDA for FY27 and EUR90-100 million over 3-4 years. Gross margin is 4-5 percentage points above Legacy, offset by higher fixed costs.

segments.name: RIECO (engineering)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR268 crore (+17.5%) and EBITDA turned to INR10 crore from negative INR17 crore on restructuring and project cost control. Management says transformation is not finished and numbers have not improved as expected.

EUR90-100 million acquired-group EBITDA targeted over the next 3-4 years, driven by synergies, value capture and sales growth; no investment needed for that volume.
Legacy Sudarshan growth of 8-10% expected in FY27; healthy margins targeted.

Acquisition debt repayment is ballooning, starting FY27 and stepping up; management expects EBITDA to cover it.

Tax: ETR is somewhat high for the acquired group due to conservative accounting and deferred taxes not recognised in some entities; similar range expected for FY27.
Annualised depreciation after final PPA is about INR347 crore.
capex_capacity: Enough capacity headroom in both Legacy and acquired plants to grow; the 3-4 year EBITDA plan needs no volume-driven investment.
Some commodity production moved from Frankfurt to the Indian Heubach site at Roha; Frankfurt is being kept for specialty products.
Legacy Indian plants debottlenecked after expansion; management did not give a utilisation percentage.
Management is exploring disposal of non-core assets; thinking is at an early stage.
Captive energy cost is 6-7% of revenue post-increase, per management.
demand_pricing: Q4 volumes recovered sharply; management says growth came from volume (customers ending destocking and buying again), with no price increases in Q4.
Management says Q4 was not industry growth but a recovery from winning back customers; pigment industry growth is about 3-4% globally, tracking GDP.
Near-term demand is described as muted due to the Middle East conflict, customers cutting inventory building and complementary products being unavailable; US housing and paint markets are weak.

Management says it does not want to profit from price rises and is passing through only the cost increases.

qa_highlights.answer: The EUR29 million cut is done; a further EUR15-20 million reduction is targeted gradually, which management sees as the normal state, when reported and business EBITDA should converge.

qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said acquired-group debt will be serviced from its cash flows, and the repayment schedule is ballooning, starting this year and stepping up.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q4 was not restocking; customers resumed buying after destocking ended, with broad recovery across segments, mainly coatings.

qa_highlights.question: Why did depreciation fall to about INR50 crore in Q4, and what is the run rate?
qa_highlights.answer: The final PPA gave a one-time depreciation reduction after fair-valuing fixed assets; the annualised depreciation run rate is about INR347 crore.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the FY27 EUR35 million EBITDA guide comes from integration versus recovery?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is a mix of value capture and recovery, with only moderate growth assumed given the geopolitical situation.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Legacy business's healthy margin sustainable through raw material volatility?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects to maintain healthy Legacy margins by passing cost increases through to customers.

Possible disposal of non-core assets is at an early stage.

506655|2026-09.headline: Sudarshan Q2 FY27 Legacy pigment revenue rose to INR821 crore (from INR651 crore), with total pigment business EBITDA at INR242 crore; Acquired Group FY27 guidance reaffirmed at EUR700m revenue and EUR35m EBITDA.
506655|2026-09.overview: Management reported a stronger Q2 FY27, with Legacy Sudarshan pigment revenue of INR821 crore (EBITDA INR128 crore, 15.6%) and total pigment global business revenue of INR2,695 crore with business EBITDA of INR242 crore versus INR2,327 crore and INR90 crore a year earlier. The VP4 raw material business was sold for EUR75.8 million (closed 2 November 2026) and proceeds are earmarked for debt reduction, while net debt stood at INR580 crore at September end before those proceeds. RIECO was a weak spot, with Q2 revenue of INR47 crore and negative EBITDA of INR3 crore due to internal supply-chain bottlenecks and cost overruns on two late-stage projects. Management kept the Acquired Group guidance unchanged despite H1 progress, citing caution on demand and a first normal full-year cycle post-acquisition.

Business EBITDA INR112 crore; reported EBITDA INR134 crore after INR22 crore inventorised overhead

segments.name: Legacy Sudarshan pigments
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR821 crore with EBITDA INR128 crore (15.6%); H1 revenue up 26% with 16.5% business EBITDA margin. Management split growth roughly equally between price and volume, with some Q2 sales pulled forward from October ahead of SAP go-live.

segments.name: Acquired Group (ex-Heubach)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR1,962 crore with business EBITDA INR112 crore; H1 business EBITDA margin 6.1% versus 2% a year ago. Growth was almost entirely price, with muted volume growth.

segments.name: RIECO
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR47 crore and EBITDA negative INR3 crore, attributed to internal supply-chain execution issues. Two late-stage projects had cost overruns fully accounted for in Q2.

segments.name: Aluminium dyes (Clariant toll manufacturing)
segments.commentary: Definitive agreements signed to acquire the manufacturing business from Clariant, including a Swiss site; closing expected early next year. Management cited product-approval sensitivity to site.

guidance_outlook: Acquired Group FY27 guidance reaffirmed at EUR700 million revenue and EUR35 million EBITDA, already net of the VP4 divestment EBITDA loss; management said H1 run-rate is already near EUR35 million.
Management expects demand signs towards Q4 FY27, though not immediate; European manufacturing index has moved positively and some raw material prices have stabilised.
SAP integration (one system from four) expected to complete by mid-FY28; wave one (Sudarshan legacy and Heubach India) is live.
Europe headcount restructuring costs INR74 crore; management expects annual savings similar to or slightly above that amount, phased in over about 1.5 years from the year-end agreement.

Value capture target of EUR90-100 million over three to four years was referenced by an analyst; management cited backward integration, AI and further purchasing and manufacturing savings as the remaining levers.
Board is evaluating capital allocation options including buybacks, with a full plan expected in about a year; no decision announced.
capex_capacity: VP4 raw material business sold to a customer for EUR75.8 million; closed 2 November 2026 with funds fully received. Captive use retained by Sudarshan is 5-10% of volume, single-digit.
Clariant aluminium dyes toll manufacturing being converted to ownership via definitive agreements, including a Swiss site; closing expected early next year.
Some products the Acquired Group makes in Europe are not yet made in India; transfer would require new physical capacity investment (IP exists, but no physical assets in India for these molecules).
Production of commoditised products has moved to India, but management said full commercialisation and cost benefit has not yet been realised.
demand_pricing: Overall US housing and European construction remain weak; masterbatch demand volatile due to oil and polymer price swings.
Customer destocking is over per management, but customers are buying only as needed; demand remains muted amid geopolitical uncertainty.

Lead times for raw materials and finished-goods deliveries have lengthened, leading to inventory build; inventory absolute level up about 25% versus 31 March 2026 per analyst; management said inventory days still improved versus H1 FY26.
Win-back of lost global key accounts (mainly Europe and US-headquartered) is underway, with business returning in coatings and digital inks; losses were spread across multiple competitors.
Innovation pipeline reopened with launches in cosmetics, cell phone and digital ink applications, plus heavy-metal-free dyes and colourants for recycled plastics; new products are margin-accretive.

qa_highlights.question: How much of revenue improvement is volume versus price, and has lost share from the Heubach insolvency period been regained?
qa_highlights.answer: Legacy Sudarshan growth split roughly half price and half volume, excluding some SAP-related pull-forward sales from October into September. Acquired Group growth was almost all price with muted volume. Management said win-backs are ongoing with global key accounts.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Acquired Group FY27 EBITDA guidance not upgraded when H1 is about two-thirds done, and is VP4 EBITDA loss included?
qa_highlights.answer: VP4 loss is included in the retained EUR35 million guidance. Management said it is being cautious because this is the first normal full-year cycle post-acquisition; it does not expect a Q3-like weak quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Captive use of VP4 product: 5% earlier versus 10% in the deck?
qa_highlights.answer: Management clarified captive use is between 5% and 10%, depending on demand, and in single digits.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Europe restructuring cost INR74 crore and what are savings and timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Restructuring affects support functions, not direct manufacturing. Annual savings expected similar to or slightly above INR74 crore, phasing in over about 1.5 years.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company buy back shares or use cash, given expected net cash?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the board, not the promoter group, is evaluating options; a full capital-allocation plan is expected in about a year. VP4 proceeds will go to debt reduction.

qa_highlights.question: What levers close the margin gap from about 6-6.5% toward 9-10% on EUR90-100 million EBITDA?
qa_highlights.answer: Achieved so far: org structure cuts, manufacturing yield and utility savings, global purchasing. Pending: backward integration, AI use, production shifts to India, and one to two percentage points from volume recovery.

qa_highlights.question: Destocking status and inventory increase?
qa_highlights.answer: Customer destocking is over. Inventory rose because of longer raw material and finished-goods lead times and demand variability; days still improved versus H1 FY26.

qa_highlights.question: Confidence in outgrowing a 3-4% global pigment market, given FY29 aspiration of about 9% growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said two-thirds of EBITDA growth aspiration comes from internal cost reduction and one-third from sales growth, driven by regaining lost business.

risks_watch: Acquired Group FY27 EBITDA guidance (EUR35 million) left unchanged despite strong H1; watch whether Q3 and Q4 deliver run-rate.
RIECO execution issues and cost overruns on two late-stage projects; negative Q2 EBITDA.
Inventory up about 25% from 31 March 2026 with rising lead times; working-capital target of further EUR15-20 million reduction in FY27 is at risk.
Win-back of lost global key accounts is ongoing and not yet quantified; FY29 growth aspiration (about 9%) is well above the 3-4% industry rate.
Clariant aluminium dye site closing and the SAP integration (mid-FY28) carry execution risk.
Capital allocation (buyback, merger with Sudarshan Colorants) remains undecided; no timeline beyond about one year.
506655|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on operational turnaround and EBITDA gains, but cautious on the outlook: management repeatedly cited weak European and US demand, geopolitics and freight costs as reasons not to raise guidance. Answers on the RIECO issues, inventory build and FY29 growth targets were more general, and several questions on capital allocation and the merger with Sudarshan Colorants were deferred.

We don't expect such a subdued quarter this quarter, but we are tending cautiously because this is the first normal two, three quarter, which we are going to experience as we have acquired this business.

506687|2026-06.headline: Transpek Q1 FY27 revenue fell 6.5% YoY to INR155.1 crore and EBITDA fell 32.4% to INR24.1 crore, with a 15.6% margin.
506687|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue was INR155.1 crore, down 6.5% YoY, with EBITDA of INR24.1 crore (down 32.4% YoY) and a 15.6% margin, and PAT of INR8.9 crore. Management attributed the decline to aggressive pricing, oversupply and subdued export demand. The company remains net debt-free. Management said it is moving to a more aggressive growth stance, with an Odisha greenfield site (INR250 crore over 5-6 years, subject to board approval) and a multi-purpose pilot plant at Ekalbara. The DuPont contract, now assigned to Arclin, continues on unchanged terms, with renewal talks expected between Q4 CY26 and Q1 CY27.

segments.name: Polymers (end-user application)
segments.commentary: Largest end-user segment at 48.7% of Q1 revenue; down from 60-65% a few years ago to roughly 45-50% over time as the portfolio diversified.

segments.name: Specialty chemicals
segments.commentary: 22.5% of Q1 revenue.

segments.name: Pharma
segments.commentary: 10.11% of Q1 revenue.

segments.name: Others
segments.commentary: 18.7% of Q1 revenue; management cited rising contribution from organic peroxides, dyes and surfactants during the quarter.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at least 15% over FY26 (about 15-20% stated), with acid chloride sales to rise from about INR4 crore to about INR15 crore this year.
Target to double business size in 5 years; management said the strategy is finalised.
EBITDA margin guided at 15-20% going forward, with product-wise margins varying.

New products: one product expected to add about INR50 crore annual revenue, with commercialisation near year-end FY27 and revenue from next year; a second product expected to add about INR50 crore annually; several others could add INR50-100 crore each.
Odisha greenfield project: board decision targeted within 25-30 days; construction could start by end-November 2026 if approved; commercial production 1.5-2 years after start; payback 4-5 years.
Multi-purpose pilot plant at Ekalbara: 6-7 months to build, around February 2027.
Management said the company expects to run all four sites at full permitted capacity this quarter.
capex_capacity: Odisha greenfield capex of about INR250 crore over 5-6 years in multiple phases, pending board approval and feasibility study; DuPont-linked capex in the past was about INR110 crore.
Multi-purpose pilot plant (four streams, multi-step chemistry, fluorination, distillation) being built at Ekalbara; about 6-7 months to complete.
Effective capacity utilisation of about 70-75% (best case 80-82%) because capacity is product-specific and permits are 20-30% below the sum of stream capacities.
Expansion blocked at Ekalbara (about 10 years of approvals pending) and Dahej (about 1.5 years for permissions). Of three job-work sites, two are in the same Ekalbara area.
Management said about INR200 crore of capex over the last 5-6 years was largely replacement and captive thionyl chloride capacity, not growth capex.
demand_pricing: Pricing pressure from Indian and global competitors; price erosion in some products. Open-market acid chloride pricing is competitive, while Arclin pricing is formula-based cost-plus.

Arclin (ex-DuPont) contract assigned in full with the same terms. Management said Arclin's order volumes are rising this quarter, and the contract is a pass-through for raw materials; rupee depreciation is passed on to the customer.
Management said it is in talks with about 2 customers on sizeable contracts, but decisions are being delayed.
Electronics-grade trimethylbenzoyl chloride (TMBC/246 TMBC, for photoinitiators) is being developed for one large customer; purification work is ongoing.
Management said there were no product discontinuations, though some product demand fell sharply in certain quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Growth has lagged the 10-12% CAGR previously guided (FY19 revenue INR595 crore vs FY26 INR621 crore, EBITDA INR117 crore vs INR80 crore); would the company consider a buyback?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said estimates are not guaranteed due to cycles, guided at least 15% revenue growth for FY27, and said the board sees buybacks as lower-return than reinvesting in growth.

qa_highlights.question: What happens if the Arclin/DuPont contract is not renewed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it sees no reason for non-renewal (nine-year supplier, no rejected kilos, no missed deliveries) but is preparing for a worst case; a non-renewal would be a significant blow to volume and margins, with recovery taking time.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the INR300 crore Silox investment not being monetised?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the stake is illiquid under the shareholder agreement; the partner has been offered the stake but has not bought it, and no near-term resolution is expected.

qa_highlights.question: What is the US tariff advantage?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no special tariff; Transpek pays the normal 18% rate, and customers receive duty drawbacks.

qa_highlights.question: Why expand capacity when utilisation is only 70-75%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said permissions at Ekalbara are blocked, product-specific streams require a mix, and Odisha is needed for new products.

qa_highlights.question: Is capex now being committed ahead of demand, and what revenue do the new products add?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is investing partly ahead of demand. It said two products could add about INR50 crore each annually, and that the INR150-200 crore guided earlier had not yet materialised.

qa_highlights.question: What is the expected IRR or payback on the INR250 crore Odisha project?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said payback would be 4-5 years.

risks_watch: Arclin/DuPont renewal (talks expected Q4 CY26 to Q1 CY27); the contract is a large share of volume and margins.
Margin pressure from competition and from volatile raw material prices (management cited a jump from about $2,600/t to $4,000/t within 10 days).
Odisha board approval and permit timing; the 2 to 1.5 year execution timeline is long.
New product commercialisation has slipped in the past (a battery electrolyte product was stopped after a technology change).
Silox stake (about INR300 crore) remains illiquid with no near-term monetisation.
Management said the West Asia conflict and logistics are a risk to global demand.

506767|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue and profit were flat (within ±1% YoY); management sees margin improvement next year but guides only 5-10% volume growth.
506767|2026-03.overview: Management described FY26 as challenging, with both top line and bottom line roughly flat YoY, and volume down about 1% and prices down about 1%. The March 2026 ammonia sourcing disruption from the Middle East war was short-lived, with inventories bridging the gap and plants kept running at roughly 60-85% utilisation. Ammonia cost rose from about INR50/kg to over INR100/kg, and the company passed through price increases, with aceto prices now above INR200/kg versus about INR140-150/kg last year. Management believes the margin trough has passed but cautioned that gains from price pass-through are temporary and that competition will settle margins later.

financial_highlights.value: Roughly flat; combined volume and price decline about 2%
About 1% above last year; capacity 2 lakh tons, output about 110,000 tons per analyst estimate (not confirmed by management)

financial_highlights.change: Up roughly 30-40% from last year's average of INR140-150/kg
Up from about INR50/kg before the war

segments.name: Ethylamines
segments.commentary: Margins have improved as alcohol prices rose and prices stabilised; management says the market is a duopoly with Balaji and has enough capacity for 4-5 years. Market share is stable.

segments.name: Methylamines
segments.commentary: Still under pressure from new capacity: Aarti Industries commissioned a plant, taking the domestic players to four (RCF, Balaji, Aarti, Alkyl Amines). Management expects overcapacity and low utilisation to persist for some time.

segments.name: Acetonitrile (aceto)
segments.commentary: Anti-dumping duty came into effect only towards end-FY26 after Chinese pipeline imports. Chinese prices have risen and imports fallen in the last quarter, with market share gains. Company has about 30,000 tons capacity across two plants and says it will be the lowest-cost producer.

segments.name: End-user mix
segments.commentary: Pharma is 50-60% of sales and agro 15-20%, together about 70-75%. Management sees no pharma slowdown yet but flagged agro risk from a possible El Nino monsoon.

guidance_outlook: Volume growth guided at 5-10% for the next year, in line with expected industry growth of about 5-7%; value growth higher because of elevated prices.
Management expects some margin improvement next year, but says it is difficult to predict continued growth beyond that.
Raw material and finished goods prices are not expected to return to pre-February 2026 levels soon; supply-chain normalisation is expected to take 3-6 months.
Kurkumbh project commissioning slipped to the beginning of Q2 FY27 from April-June 2026; mechanical completion expected by end-June; economics unchanged.
FY27-28 capex estimated at INR80-90 crore, mainly the balance of the Dahej new product plant and engineering projects; maintenance capex INR20-30 crore per year.
A product launch from the R&D pipeline is expected in July 2026; further R&D investment decisions deferred until volatility settles.
capex_capacity: Capacity utilisation at most plants is about 60-85%; enough capacity for the next few years without new investment in existing products.
Ethylamines: large plant built 3-4 years ago, adequate for 4-5 years of growth; debottlenecking possible.
Acetonitrile: about 30,000 tons capacity across two plants, sufficient for a couple of years. Balaji is building an 18,000 ton ACN plant this year.
Kurkumbh project delayed by about one quarter; mechanical completion expected end-June 2026.
Dahej new product plant: remaining spend in FY27 within the INR80-90 crore capex plan.
demand_pricing: Ammonia supply was disrupted for a week or two in March 2026, but sourcing recovered and inventories covered the gap; ammonia contracts are now short-term because suppliers are reluctant to commit longer.

Price increases have been passed through, with customers absorbing them because the company's products are a minor (C-item) cost in their bill of materials. Management believes competition, not customers, is the main pricing pressure.
Margin widening from inventory of cheaper raw materials is temporary; management expects margins to settle at competitive levels after one to two months.
Chinese imports of acetonitrile fell after Chinese players raised prices; the anti-dumping duty took effect only towards end-FY26.
Methylamines face overcapacity after Aarti's commissioning; ethylamines margins have recovered.
Peptides and acetonitrile demand expected to grow, but the company sees much of the optimistic peptide demand forecasts as unproven.

qa_highlights.question: How has user demand held up after raw material-driven price increases, and what is expected next?
qa_highlights.answer: Management has not yet seen demand destruction. Its products are a minor cost for customers, so pressure is expected from competition rather than customers. Prices are unlikely to revert to pre-February levels soon.

qa_highlights.question: Is ammonia available broadly across the industry, and how does this affect spreads?
qa_highlights.answer: Ammonia rose from about INR50/kg to over INR100/kg. Government allocation is expected, as aliphatic industry needs only 10,000-15,000 tons per month. Stabilisation is expected in 3-6 months, and any spread gain is temporary.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for capacity utilisation and the Balaji and Aarti capacity additions?
qa_highlights.answer: Utilisation is 60-85%. Methylamines are overcapacity after Aarti's entry, which is expected to take a long time to absorb. Ethylamines have adequate capacity for 4-5 years. Balaji's 18,000 ton ACN plant will add competition, but the company believes it is the lowest-cost producer.

qa_highlights.question: What is the planned capex for FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex is about INR80-90 crore, mainly completing the Dahej plant and engineering projects. Apart from this, there is no major planned capex for existing products; maintenance capex is about INR20-30 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company diversifying ammonia sourcing or looking at green ammonia?
qa_highlights.answer: Ammonia is bought mainly through distributors linked to fertiliser plants, with direct manufacturer links in only one or two cases. Green ammonia is still 3-5 years away from cost parity.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the margin improvement is structural versus temporary?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects some margin improvement next year. It noted that margins widen temporarily when raw material prices rise and fall, and that the company cannot predict whether it will keep growing.

risks_watch: Ammonia availability and price, with contracts now short-term and the Middle East war (Hormuz Strait) unresolved.
Demand response to 30-40% higher prices; agro demand at risk from a possible El Nino monsoon.
Methylamines overcapacity after Aarti's entry, with no near-term recovery expected.
Balaji's 18,000 ton acetonitrile plant and possible Chinese re-entry as import pricing normalises.
Pass-through reversal: competition may pull prices down faster than costs fall, reducing the temporary margin gain.

506879|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 22.1% YoY to INR43.8 crore and EBITDA margin hit 47.5%, while the company pursues a debt- and equity-funded acquisition of MicroBiopharm Japan and Sanofi brands.

Management described the business as sold out in capacity for years and said the expanded fermentation capacity (about 540 KL, roughly doubling capacity) starts full operation by end-August 2026. qa_highlights.question: How does the INR3,000 crore acquisition make sense given interest costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Sanofi deal is expected to close later, with long-stop June 2027, and that interest rates in the target geographies are much lower than 10%. It said the business is cash-flow positive from the start.

qa_highlights.question: What is the funding structure for the MBJ and Sanofi deals?

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex plan for the base business in FY27?

qa_highlights.question: What is the path from Sanofi brands to manufacturing?

qa_highlights.question: Why was the Themis Medicare merger withdrawn?

507205|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 net revenue rose 148% YoY to INR 949 crore and EBITDA margin was 16.3%, with Imperial Blue consolidated; FY27 guided to 16-18% combined EBITDA margin.
507205|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 volumes rose 135% YoY to over 8 million cases, of which Imperial Blue (IB) contributed 4.6 million cases, while ex-IB volumes were roughly flat as Andhra Pradesh base effects reversed. Reported net revenue was INR 949 crore (INR 941 crore subsidy-adjusted) and EBITDA was INR 155 crore at a 16.3% margin, or INR 146 crore and 15.5% subsidy-adjusted. Management changed presentation so trade discounts and schemes are netted from gross revenue, which lowers reported revenue and gross margin but lifts EBITDA and PAT margins without changing absolute figures. FY27 guidance covers high-single to low-double digit volume growth and a 16-18% combined EBITDA margin over 24-36 months.

Mainly TSMA fees and labour code impact

segments.commentary: Ex-IB volumes were flat in Q4 against a high Andhra Pradesh base from the route-to-market change in Oct/Nov 2024; secondary sales grew about 5%. FY26 ex-IB volume was 13.6 million cases, up 14%.

Capex about INR 25 crore each in FY27 and FY28, maintenance only.

Q1 FY27 margins expected to see some short-term pressure from input cost inflation.

qa_highlights.question: What is the IB run rate and the growth outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: IB growth should be similar to or slightly above the combined business because of its lower FY26 base; Maharashtra impact is largely in the FY26 base.

qa_highlights.answer: Gross debt is less relevant because of a 2-year moratorium; net debt is expected at about INR 1,700 crore by March 2027, with upside bias.

qa_highlights.answer: Management uses 15.5% as the base. The full year should hold the guided range, but Q1 FY27 faces input cost inflation, so no Q1 expansion is expected.

qa_highlights.question: Will TSMA costs keep hitting operating expenses after transition?

507514|2026-03.headline: FY26 consolidated revenue fell 14.8% to INR1,233 crore and EBITDA to INR89.7 crore after the Bhopal licence suspension; FY27 guided at INR1,400-1,500 crore.
507514|2026-03.overview: FY26 was a difficult year: consolidated revenue fell 14.8% to INR1,233 crore, EBITDA declined to INR89.7 crore and PAT was INR10.2 crore. Beer volumes dropped 20% to 187.19 lakh cases, driven by the temporary licence suspension at the Bhopal plant and weak demand in Karnataka and Odisha, while IMFL grew 32% to 15.03 lakh cases. Management said the Bhopal licence renewal is pending with authorities, with no definite timeline; the UP greenfield brewery has begun trials and commercial production is expected from June 2026. Management guided FY27 revenue to INR1,400-1,500 crore and FY27 EBITDA margin to close to 10%, with FY28 guidance deferred about six months.

segments.commentary: Volumes grew 32% to 15.03 lakh cases in FY26, led by premium portfolio penetration. Mahavat Whisky was launched in the mid-premium segment, and supply was halted when Bhopal stopped.

segments.commentary: Management said roughly 50% of company volume historically came from Bhopal. Production has been halted since February and Delhi, UP and Jharkhand supplies from this plant stopped; finished goods were cleared and sold.

demand_pricing: Karnataka (about 30-35% of business) is improving after the state's excise duty rationalisation, which lowered MRP on mainstream and economy beer; management says it is gaining share over the last 3-4 quarters.
Industry volume in April and May 2026 grew about 15-16% combined, with April at 51-52 lakh cases and May at about 50 lakh cases despite rain.

Andhra Pradesh business expected to start in the next 3-4 weeks; Tamil Nadu share is growing.
Input cost inflation in glass bottles, aluminium cans, barley and logistics is the main margin pressure; long-term supply contracts are not holding price.

qa_highlights.question: Revenue and EBITDA margin outlook for FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 revenue guided at INR1,400-1,500 crore, with the Bhopal licence assumed. FY27 EBITDA margin close to 10%; FY28 guidance deferred about six months.

qa_highlights.question: How much will the UP plant contribute in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: 15-20 lakh cases from UP in FY27 at roughly INR600 per case, about INR120 crore; plant capacity is 1 crore cases per annum with a 2-3 year ramp-up.

qa_highlights.question: Is Q1 FY27 going to be as loss-making as Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management expects Q1 to be better than Q4 on higher Hassan and Odisha utilisation and lower annual costs booked in Q4. Only labour cost at Bhopal will fall; no salary cuts were made.

qa_highlights.question: How long to regain Bhopal and MP market share once the plant reopens?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects to recover the similar market share within about six months, though the main season makes it harder now. Management said the sales and distribution team is ready and waiting.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a one-time impact from Karnataka's excise cut?
qa_highlights.answer: No one-time impact. The MRP cut lowers consumer prices; management said revenue would rise slightly and margins would not suffer.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the licence lost and what internal steps are being taken?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said some matters are sub judice and cannot be discussed. It is appointing a dedicated compliance officer and improving compliance processes. The company said the rating downgrades stem only from the licence suspension.

risks_watch: Bhopal licence renewal timing is open-ended. Management's timelines have slipped from days to weeks to months, and the FY27 guidance depends on it.
Input cost inflation (glass, cans, barley) with no fixed-price contracts; FY28 margin guidance deferred.
Credit rating downgrades at parent and subsidiary; management says ratings will recover once the licence is restored. About INR400 crore of undrawn lines are available.
Governance: the Company Secretary resigned (personal reasons, per management) and an internal auditor left; a compliance officer is being appointed.
Market share loss in MP and Delhi may not be fully recovered, per management's own comments.

507526|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 net revenue INR239 crores, EBITDA up 13% to INR40 crores at 17% margin; proprietary IMFL volumes up 37% YoY.

Ethanol volumes fell 35% YoY on industry oversupply, and merchant ENA volumes rose 129%. 507552|2026-03.headline: FY26 was a down year: management guides ~18% FY27 volume growth while declining to disclose EBITDA quantum; Q4 realisations fell on lower-cost 2025 crop inventory.

507552|2026-09.headline: Foods & Inns posted a forex loss of INR106 million in Q2 FY27 from forward contracts, with ~3,300 MT unshipped orders expected to clear in Q3.
507552|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 was hit by a notional forex loss of INR106 million (about INR10 crores), booked in other expenses, from forward cover on export sales as the rupee depreciated and shipments slipped. Dispatches were delayed by container unavailability and high freight rates, but October saw a substantial pickup, with about 60% of the ~3,300 MT unshipped orders shipped that month. Management said there are no cancellations, only deferrals, and expects all carry-over execution in Q3. The company has stopped booking new forward covers since April and is discussing possible bank penalties.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Rs 200 crore Nagpur capex high for a formulation plant?

qa_highlights.question: Dahej split: revenue, EBITDA, Bayer revenue and royalty?

qa_highlights.question: Channel inventory trend for Q1-Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management sees neither stocking nor destocking; inventory rotating normally with market demand; no change expected by end-Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Volume vs price split for the revenue decline?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said value -12.56% and volume about -12.7%, with price effect negligible; denied a 12% price growth in the books.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY27 crop protection flattish given biologicals?

risks_watch: Monsoon recovery and kharif sowing: June rainfall deficit about 40% narrowed to about 15% by end-July, and management said reservoir levels are significantly depleted; FY27 small single-digit growth guidance depends on Q2 and Q3 rain.

Bayer-acquired molecules: no revenue booked in Q1 for overseas markets, FY27 contribution not quantified, and Iprovalicarb sales are expected from September; distribution in some markets still being set up.
Dahej synthesis site: FY27 revenue guided about Rs 65 crore and EBITDA about negative Rs 4-5 crore; breakeven described as difficult.

Nagpur plant: outlay up to Rs 200 crore with capex of about Rs 100 crore-plus in FY27-28 cited by CFO; asset-turn assumption (7x-8x) not confirmed and to be revisited around late Q4; commissioning targeted for Q4 FY28.

Biologicals: three products with the third due by end-August 2026, and state approval tightening; the bio-stimulant revenue target was not given and the category is being reworked. A GST notice is also pending, with the company confident of winning but no timeline given.

We are still pretty hopeful of the growth that will come in Q2 and Q3, and yet it is absolutely appropriate that we project a clear picture to our investors.

507717|2026-09.headline: Dhanuka Q2 FY27 revenue rose 9.91% to INR657.51 crore, but management reiterated only a low-single-digit full-year growth and ~100 bps gross margin loss.
507717|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations grew about 9.9% YoY to INR657.51 crore, with EBITDA of INR152.97 crore and PAT of INR109.22 crore, both up YoY. Growth was driven by insecticides (47% of revenue), which management attributed to El Niño-led product focus and channel agility rather than market share gains. Management said Q2 growth is not a run-rate: it expects low single-digit revenue growth for the full year, with Q3 and Q4 subdued and gross margin down about 100 bps. Analysts probed channel inventory, margin drivers, Dahej plant ramp-up and the new-product index, and management was specific on most points but declined product-level revenue figures.

segments.name: Zones (share of Q2 turnover)
segments.commentary: North 31%, East 12%, West 28%, South 29%. Analyst noted North grew about 22% in Q2 and about 12% in H1; management attributed North strength to irrigated markets.

segments.name: Product categories (share of Q2 revenue)
segments.commentary: Insecticides 47%, fungicides 25%, herbicides 8%, others 20%. Herbicides were hit by dry weather; insecticides grew strongly.

segments.name: Dahej (Harsh Dhanuka)
segments.commentary: Plant at about 70% utilisation per analyst; H1 sales about INR55 crore and H1 EBITDA loss about INR1.79 crore. Two new fungicide products planned in the existing plant, taking the portfolio from 2 to 4 products in FY28; capex amount not disclosed.

guidance_outlook: Full-year FY27 revenue growth now guided at low single digit (management clarified this after earlier single-digit guidance; a Q2 growth of about 10% is not a run-rate for Q3 and Q4).
Gross margin expected to fall about 100 bps for the year, with EBITDA decline similar or slightly larger; management said margin expansion will not happen this year.
Q3 and Q4 described as subdued; management does not expect a high sales season in Q3.
Rabi season initial movement described as promising in certain regions; South and East zones are the key for Rabi.
Management said the GST refund effect on gross margin recurs every quarter; excluding it, gross margin is flat.
Biostimulant Dhanzyme Gold liquid formulation approved, launch planned for December 2026.
Dahej capacity expansion approved; new fungicides to be added in FY28. Capex quantum to be clarified in a later round.
Two plant growth regulator and growth influencer launches planned in Q3.
capex_capacity: Dahej plant at about 70% utilisation; capacity expansion of existing products approved along with 2 new fungicide products in the existing plant (FY28).
Capex quantum not disclosed; management said clarity will come in a later round but the company is 'absolutely committed' to capex.
Two R&D centres with NABL-accredited labs; partnerships with 10 multinational agrochemical innovators from Japan, Europe and the US.
Distribution footprint: over 10 million farmers reached via 6,500 distributors, 80,000-plus retailers and 40-plus warehouses.
demand_pricing: Q2 growth attributed to insecticides (LaNevo, Miyako, Mortar, Decis), plant growth regulators and nutritional products; management said this was product-specific, not market share gain.
Chilli in South and cotton (repeat insecticide sprays) and vegetables in East supported demand; fungicide demand was weak.

Generic crop pricing under severe pressure; management said tepid demand prevents full pass-through of raw material cost increases. Some raw materials fell in Q2 and others rose; increases passed on selectively.

Channel inventory described as optimal; company said it cleans channel monthly and did not front-load in Q1. Analyst asked about receivables jump; management said debtors are not aggressively placed and material is taken back quickly.

Farmer purchasing power constrained: commodity prices high but rainfall-dependent farmers reduced, per management; fertiliser e-Token and enforcement cited as reducing fertiliser-linked tagging of crop protection sales.
Polin (paddy fungicide from Nippon Soda, Japan) priced above market acceptance; not expected to scale near term.
Brazil and European subsidiaries are for registration only; customers appointed in about 14 countries, purchase orders in hand from 5.

qa_highlights.question: What drove about 10% growth in Q2 and was there regional share gain?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it was product-specific insecticide growth from El Niño-driven re-planning, plus focus on water-available areas and no Q1 channel front-loading. Q2 growth is not an indicator for the next two quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 10% growth a run-rate, and will growth moderate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management maintained single-digit growth guidance for the year, saying Q2 growth reflects the weak base of last year's same quarter and is not indicative of Q3 and Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Is the strong North performance (about 22% in Q2) market share gain or industry-driven?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said North irrigated markets (Punjab, Haryana, Western UP) were industry's favourite; it would not confirm share gain.

qa_highlights.question: Gross margin held despite lowest ITI and high-margin mix moderation: what drove it?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said gross margin was slightly lower YoY due to GST refund effects; EBITDA margin improved mainly from tighter other expenses. Value growth (10%) exceeded volume growth (6%).

qa_highlights.question: Full-year guidance: high single digit or double digit?
qa_highlights.answer: Rahul Dhanuka said the company will grow by a single low digit for the year, with gross margin down about 100 bps and EBITDA down similarly or slightly more.

qa_highlights.question: Will product-level revenue such as LaNevo be disclosed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to share product-specific revenue, though it said LaNevo was a leading growth driver in Q2.

risks_watch: Full-year guidance cut to low single-digit growth; Q3 and Q4 subdued, with weak demand in the Western and Central regions where rain opportunity has ended.
Gross margin pressure of about 100 bps; competitors' high-cost inventory could pressure generic pricing in H2.
Dahej remains loss-making; capex quantum and timelines for the two new fungicides not yet disclosed.
Enforcement against unregistered and spurious products; industry-wide concern flagged, with FICCI involvement.
Rabi season performance in South and East zones is the key swing factor.
New-product index (ITI) moderation; Polin unlikely to scale near term, pipeline depends on Q3 PGR launches and Dhanzyme Gold December launch.

So this 10% growth is not an indication of what we can expect in other two quarters.
So about 100 bps less in gross margin.
I think so the position is that we'll be growing by a single low digit, and that is where we are.

507779|2026-03.headline: Kanpur Plastipack Q4 FY26 standalone PAT rose ~14% YoY to INR14.53 crore, but a INR3.65 crore DFIA income reversal cut other operating income to negative INR2.9 crore.
507779|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 standalone total income was INR183.1 crore (up ~6.16% YoY), with EBITDA of INR25.06 crore (13.69% margin) and PAT of INR14.53 crore. FY26 total income rose 26.26% to INR726.67 crore, EBITDA reached INR74.75 crore (10.29% margin) and PAT was INR38.19 crore (up ~68%). Management attributed the Q4 hit to government suspension of import duty on polypropylene until 30 June, which removed the value of DFIA licences. rows.why: About 92% of the portfolio is outside NLEM price control, allowing up to 9.9% increases, and price contributed 6-7% of Jagsonpal's growth against ~5-7% for the market.

tone.note: Management was confident about the Q4 turnaround, the 1.5x IPM target and the buyback, but gave vague segment and therapy detail and was evasive on capital allocation; analysts pressed on sustainability and the use of surplus cash.

507789|2026-06.headline: Jagsonpal Q1 FY27 revenue rose about 9% YoY to Rs.82 crores, with operating EBITDA up 21% to nearly Rs.19 crores and PAT up 22% to Rs.13 crores.
507789|2026-06.overview: Management said the growth seen from Q4 FY26 carried into Q1 FY27, with revenue up about 9% YoY and gross margin above 65%. Operating EBITDA margin expanded about 240 bps to above 23% and PAT margin rose 176 bps to 16%. The company completed the Rs.40 crore buyback and acquired 85% of Aequitas Healthcare for Rs.20.8 crores (enterprise value about Rs.25 crores) to enter the hospital segment. Management guided Aequitas to Rs.10 crores EBITDA by year two post-integration, though analysts questioned the step-up from about Rs.50 lakh EBITDA in FY26.

financial_highlights.change: after Rs.40 crore buyback (about half added back to cash)

segments.name: Branded prescription (core)
segments.commentary: Power brand portfolio grew 19% vs market 16%; five brands are #1 in their molecules and 14 are in the top five. Maintane (Pharmarack ~Rs.46 crores: injections Rs.34 crores, tablets Rs.13 crores) is one of the top three brands. Management is shifting mix from acute to semi-chronic and specialty therapies; new brand run-rates have almost doubled.

segments.name: Aequitas Healthcare (hospital pharma, 85% owned)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue Rs.53 crores and EBITDA about Rs.50 lakh per analyst. Portfolio is ICU and perioperative injectables, including latest-generation antibiotics, all branded, sold to corporate hospital chains (no government tenders). Management targets about Rs.100 crores revenue in FY28-FY29 and Rs.10 crores+ EBITDA by year two; gross margins are structurally thinner than JPL's branded business.

guidance_outlook: Target to grow at 1.5x industry growth rate in coming quarters (management reiterated on Pharmarack vs secondary-sales variance question).
Aequitas: about Rs.100 crores business within two and a half years (FY28-FY29) and Rs.10 crores+ EBITDA by year two post-integration; synergies expected over 36 months.
Productivity target of upward of Rs.2,50,000 per-person productivity (PCPM varies by vertical).
Dividend of 200% recommended, including 75% special dividend, subject to AGM approval.
Aequitas expected to contribute meaningfully from second year onwards; numbers expected to show in about the next two quarters.
capex_capacity: Aequitas acquired as a subsidiary (not a BTA route); working capital cycle is longer than JPL and will not be aligned with JPL.
Aequitas network: about 49 institutional medical representatives, access to over 1,000 hospitals, around 50 hospitals contribute the majority of top line.
Lean and green productivity programme rolled out company-wide in Q1.
demand_pricing: Secondary (Pharmarack) growth of 18.9% vs reported primary sales growth of about 9%; management attributed the gap to stockist data and geographic statistical correction, and said it is reviewing the variance.
Hospital channel pricing is price-led; management said margins are structurally thinner than in branded prescription business.
Top 10 Aequitas products are over 50% of its sales.
Management reported one first-wave product launch in Q1 and expects one more in the current quarter.
Brand focus for growth: Indocap, Maintane, Endoreg (gynae), Pru and Eukroma (derma).

qa_highlights.question: Why is reported sales growth (about 9%) far below the 18% IPM growth cited?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the data is secondary (stockist) sales and the variance is partly statistical correction for geographies; it is reviewing why the gap is so wide and reiterated the 1.5x industry growth target.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Aequitas Rs.10 crore EBITDA target achievable from Rs.50 lakh in FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited brand equity, lean team, corporate-chain focus, cross-selling of JPL brands and new-age brands with high value per patient; promoters remain with 15% and continue to run the business, so their salaries are not a one-off saving.

qa_highlights.question: Size of Maintane and its impact on portfolio growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Pharmarack value about Rs.46 crores (Rs.34 crores injections, Rs.13 crores tablets); growing ahead of molecule market; one of top three brands, but management did not disclose internal values.

qa_highlights.question: Aequitas gross margin looks low for a branded business; why?
qa_highlights.answer: In hospitals, price comes before brand, so margins are thinner; management plans mix improvement and differentiated innovative launches, but said it is too early to quantify.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the sharp working capital improvement?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it mainly to inventory control and stricter collections, and said payments now go out on due date; the big step-down was in FY22-FY24 (cash conversion cycle from 59 to 22 days).

qa_highlights.question: Any first-in-India or breakthrough molecule pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it never mentioned such a pipeline; it is targeting first-wave launches (about 5-10 companies) in gynae, ortho and derma, and launched one such product in Q1.

risks_watch: Aequitas execution: hospital working capital is longer and margins thinner; Rs.10 crore EBITDA in year two is an aggressive target from Rs.50 lakh base.
Concentration risk: Maintane and Indocap drive much of recent growth; management acknowledges the portfolio effect depends on a few brands.
Gap between secondary (Pharmarack ~18.9%) and reported primary growth (~9%) needs explanation next quarter.
Attrition and sales-force productivity: management claims improvement but gave no hard numbers.
Board change: Pallavi Dinodia Gupta stepped down; Anil Kumar Matai joined as Independent Director.

key_quotes: This 9% growth in sales has translated into a 21% growth in operating EBITDA as well as a 22% growth in net profits for the company.
Aequitas alone, we are looking at around Rs.100 crores of business within two and a half years' time, starting from now.
Growth without margins, improvement is hollow.

rows.why: Capex was not discussed and no utilisation figure was given, so no capex call can be made.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Management reported one first-wave launch in Q1 and expects one more in the current quarter, and targets about 5-10 first-wave launches in gynae, ortho and derma.

rows.why: Management said Aequitas numbers should show in about the next two quarters, against FY26 revenue of Rs.53 crore and EBITDA of about Rs.50 lakh, with a Rs.10 crore EBITDA target by year two.

rows.why: Cash conversion cycle fell from 59 to 22 days over FY22-FY24 and management says payments now go out on due date, though Aequitas's longer working-capital cycle will not align with JPL's.

rows.label: Hospital channel pricing pressure
rows.why: Management says hospitals are price-led, Aequitas gross margins are structurally thinner, and it is too early to quantify the mix improvement it plans.

507789|2026-09.headline: Jagsonpal Q2 FY27 standalone revenue rose 9.3% YoY to INR81 crores, with H1 organic growth at 9.3% and management targeting INR100 crores quarterly revenue in Q3.
507789|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 was the first quarter with Aequitas consolidated and included the Group Pharma wellness brands from 1 October. Standalone revenue grew 9.3% YoY to INR81 crores and consolidated revenue reached INR96 crores (up 29%). Standalone EBITDA margin was 22.7% and consolidated 19.3%, with H1 EBITDA margin at 22.9%, up 40 bps. Management reiterated the INR500 crore revenue vision for FY28 on an organic basis, but admitted growth remains short of expectations and is still below the IPM rate.

financial_highlights.change: H1 64.7%, up close to 70 bps YoY

financial_highlights.metric: Consolidated net operating cash flow (H1 FY27)

segments.name: Standalone branded business (Jagsonpal)
segments.commentary: Q2 growth around 15% vs IPM ~12% in Jul-Sep 2026; H1 around 15% vs IPM ~11%. Branded prescription growing over 10%, contributing around 11-11.5% of growth. Top 10 brands are about 58% of revenue, nine ranked top 5 in their markets.

segments.name: Aequitas Healthcare (hospital and critical care, acquired July 2026)
segments.commentary: First full quarter consolidated; provides entry into corporate hospital chains, which management says now contribute over 11.5% of industry sales. Dedicated business head appointed; first value-added launch targeted for end-November with go-to-market in early December. Hospital margins are structurally lower.

segments.name: Group Pharma wellness portfolio (acquired October 2026)
segments.commentary: Two established brands (hematinics and respiratory) sold in 6 states, adding around 10,000 doctors and an approximate INR1.75 crore base. Management says margins are similar to Jagsonpal; cross-selling planned in Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh and Karnataka.

guidance_outlook: Quarterly revenue to cross INR100 crores in Q3 FY27; management said Q3 growth would be above 1.5x IPM and EBITDA-accretive.
INR500 crore revenue vision by FY28 (calendar 2028), organic only, excluding further acquisitions; management says it is aspirational but has a road map.
Blended consolidated EBITDA margin expected to return to around 22% or more; Q3 said to be above 22% and Q4 seasonally weaker.
Standalone gross margin expected to improve 50-75 bps YoY; consolidated gross margin to stay near Q2 level. Aequitas benefits from procurement and supply-chain actions expected only from Q4.
Full-year Aequitas revenue guidance of INR100 crores by FY28 unchanged. No new product launches planned in Q3 beyond the Aequitas brand; some launches planned for Q4.
capex_capacity: Asset-light model; no manufacturing capacity disclosed. Management says no manpower addition beyond budgeted numbers.
Investment in people: MR productivity up about 10%, hospital team being built to cross-sell into Aequitas network.
Management is evaluating whether to own backend (API or formulation) manufacturing for future expansion outside India; no decision yet, with the company citing ample capital flexibility.
demand_pricing: Gynaecology is the largest contributor (about 35,000 gynaecologists engaged), followed by orthopaedics and dermatology.
Maintane grew around 29% in Q2 vs molecule ~20%; Metadec ~14% vs ~13%; Lycored ~15% vs ~13%; Endoreg ~20% vs market degrowth.
Indocap grew 4.5%, about 1% below its market; Equirex is constrained by NRx restrictions. Management expects a packaging and indication innovation for Indocap in November.
Hospital contract pricing is under pressure from API price declines over the last 12 months; contracts are typically annual.
New products contributed about 2.3-2.5% of growth; in-licensing talks on 1-2 opportunities are ongoing but margins expected to be low.

qa_highlights.question: Is INR500 crore by FY28 realistic given about 10% growth and a INR75 crore acquired run-rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called it aspirational but based on organic growth with a clear road map and no further acquisitions; it cites multiple investments in launches and people, and a growth acceleration expected from Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company provide a separate organic vs inorganic growth line?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the split will be given as commentary, not a separate line. Group Pharma's contribution will be measured against the 6 states it covers, with its base around INR1.75 crores.

qa_highlights.question: Why acquire Aequitas and Group Pharma rather than deepen gynae and derma?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said few gynae or ortho targets were available or affordable. Aequitas gives hospital channel access; Group Pharma offers a culturally similar organisation, distribution in 6 states, and co-prescription brands with similar margins.

qa_highlights.question: What is the gross margin trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Standalone gross margin is close to 65% and expected to rise 50-75 bps YoY; the Aequitas hospital business is lower margin, so consolidated margin should stay close to Q2 levels.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the Pharmarack IPM figure ahead of reported growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the data is sample-based and differs from internal numbers; internal branded prescription growth is over 10%, and the gap is expected to narrow in a couple of quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Are there any issues with ramping up the Aequitas portfolio?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the ramp-up is on plan, with API-driven price pressure in hospital contracts; procurement benefits are expected to start from Q4, and full-year Aequitas revenue guidance of INR100 crores by FY28 is unchanged.

risks_watch: Organic growth of 9.3% in H1 is below the 1.5x IPM target and below management's own expectations; Q3 must show the promised acceleration.
Consolidated EBITDA margin of 19.3% against the 22% target depends on Aequitas margin improvement, which management expects only from Q4.
Pharmarack IPM data (12-16.8%) runs ahead of reported growth; management attributes this to sampling and secondary stocking, and the gap needs to close.
Hospital channel pricing pressure from API cost increases and annual contracts.
Strategic direction beyond FY28 remains undecided, including possible backend or manufacturing investment and the chronic-therapy shift, with the discussion still with promoters and the board.
Indocap (legacy brand) growing below market; Equirex constrained by NRx regulation.

507815|2026-03.headline: Gillette India FY26 sales rose 8% to ₹3,100 crore and PAT rose 23% to about ₹650 crore, with the company citing a ~300bps structural margin gain.
507815|2026-03.overview: Management reported FY26 (year ended March 31, 2026) sales of about ₹3,100 crore, up 8%, and PAT of about ₹650 crore, up 23%, attributed to productivity across cost buckets. Management said the topline slowdown was largely due to one-time export impacts from affiliate distribution changes, including the Bangladesh distribution agreement closure, and that domestic sales were growing quarter on quarter. The call focused on new launches (Gillette Guard 3in1, Gillette trimmers, Oral-B Sensitive), Venus growth, productivity, and raw material inflation linked to the West Asia conflict. Management gave no numerical FY27 guidance.

segments.name: Male grooming (Blades and Razors)
segments.commentary: Management says the category grows about 12% and Gillette remains market leader; male grooming offtake grew 8% in P6M and 12% in P12M. Gillette Guard grew double digit and premium razors grew in early teens.

segments.name: Female grooming (Venus)
segments.commentary: Venus contributes double digits to grooming and is growing upwards of 20%; female grooming overall is growing upwards of 20%. The focus is new-user growth in in-home hair removal.

segments.name: Manual oral care (Oral-B)
segments.commentary: Growing high single digits, driven by the Oral-B Sensitive range, which is growing double digit and is among the fastest growing segments in the category.

segments.name: Power oral care (Oral-B)
segments.commentary: Growing at roughly 1.5x this year and at double digits steadily; business has doubled in the last 3 years.

segments.name: Trimmers and appliances
segments.commentary: Four new Gillette trimmers launched about 2 months before the call; management expects the trimmers category to grow at early double digits.

guidance_outlook: No numerical FY27 sales or margin guidance was given; management said it expects some challenges to continue in the near term.
Management aims to grow ahead of the male grooming category and keep balancing topline and bottom-line growth.
A multi-year savings and productivity plan is in place by business unit to support margins and offset input-cost inflation.
Management said it cannot comment on future margins but expects productivity to fund investment and provide cover against macro volatility.
Management expects growth may fluctuate in the mid-term; it sees India growing at 6.5% for the year.
capex_capacity: About 85% of products are manufactured domestically; finished goods are exported to more than 10 countries.
Bhiwadi manufacturing plant issue was resolved within a few days with zero supply-related shortfall, per management.
Management is constantly assessing the locally manufactured vs imported supply chain mix.
Supply 3.0 advance ordering now covers half of the business; over 2 million automated on-shelf availability checks are run daily.
demand_pricing: Gillette Guard 3in1 (launched about 2 months earlier): about 1 million razors sold in the launch month, distribution reached over 6 lakh stores, and a new copy reached 20 crore viewers in month 1.
Numeric distribution rose by a couple of points in FY26 for priority SKUs; premium Mach3 and Fusion distribution grew at mid-single digits for 3 years.
Gillette Guard added 20 million new users over the last 3 years.
Management said raw material costs were hit by crude up ~50% and resins up ~50%, with availability challenged; the company said it did not go out of stock.
Management said rural consumption remains higher than urban, but rural is softening because of inflation.

qa_highlights.question: Why was revenue growth subdued and volatile in FY26 and the March quarter, and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said one-time export impacts from affiliate-company decisions, including the Bangladesh distribution agreement closure, weigh on the base. Excluding them, growth would roughly double, and domestic sales are growing quarter on quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Are FY26 margin gains sustainable, and what about FY27 margins and raw material inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said structural margins improved upwards of 300 bps through premium innovation and productivity. It would not comment on FY27 but said a multi-year savings plan is in place and it will keep mitigating inflation and freight overcharges.

qa_highlights.question: What is the growth plan over the next 3 to 5 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will double down on its five-vector integrated strategy: daily-use portfolio, superiority, productivity, constructive disruption and an enabled organisation. No numeric target was given.

qa_highlights.question: What are the growth drivers in Venus and female grooming?
qa_highlights.answer: Venus is double digit in grooming and growing upwards of 20%; the focus is new-user growth in in-home hair removal through influencers and myth-busting content. No Venus salience figure was disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: What is the trimmers and appliances opportunity, and what share is targeted?
qa_highlights.answer: Four trimmers were launched about 2 months before the call; the category is expected to grow at early double digits. Management aims to grow faster than the category but gave no share target.

qa_highlights.question: Was the Bhiwadi plant issue fully resolved, and were there supply challenges?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the issue was resolved within a few days, with zero supply-related challenges, and the stock exchange was alerted.

risks_watch: Input cost inflation: crude and resin up about 50%, with tight availability tied to West Asia conflict; the margin impact was not quantified.
Export revenue volatility from affiliate distribution changes, including the Bangladesh agreement closure.
Softening rural consumption and inflation-driven pressure on consumer spending.
Competition in men's shaving, which management acknowledged in Q&A without giving share data.
Next quarter: whether domestic growth and margin gains hold, and the early traction of Guard 3in1 and trimmers.
507815|2026-03.management_tone: Management was confident on the long-term record and category growth, but cautious on near-term challenges from inflation and supply costs. It deflected several quantitative questions (FY27 margins, share targets, Venus salience, the innovation pipeline) and said some information would be withheld as price sensitive.
key_quotes: We have consistently grown topline AND bottom-line for the last 5 years!
Gillette continues to be the market leader in the Blades and Razors segment, and we have grown year on year.
As an example, crude has been highly volatile and prices have gone up by 50%. As an outcome, resins have gone up by about 50% as well.
Despite these significant disruptions, we have not gone out of stock… or made compromises on product performance.

rows.why: No numerical FY27 guidance was given and management expects some challenges to continue in the near term.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade

rows.when: already launched; traction through next 2-3 quarters
rows.why: Four new Gillette trimmers launched about 2 months before the call and Gillette Guard 3in1 launched about 2 months earlier with about 1 million razors sold in launch month.

rows.why: Management said it will keep mitigating inflation and freight overcharges under a multi-year savings plan, but gave no pricing figure and the crude and resin rise is ~50%.

rows.why: The Bangladesh distribution agreement closure is a one-time export drag on the base; management said excluding it growth would roughly double, but the closure itself is not reversing.

rows.why: Supply 3.0 advance ordering now covers half the business and over 2 million automated on-shelf checks run daily, supporting availability through the input shortage.

508814|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 consolidated sales rose 37% to Rs 1,021 crore and EBITDA rose 53% to Rs 130 crore, with net debt cut to Rs 1,159 crore.
508814|2026-03.overview: Cosmo First reported Q4 FY26 consolidated sales of Rs 1,021 crore (up 37% YoY on 41% volume growth) and EBITDA of Rs 130 crore (up 53% from Rs 85 crore), helped by new BOPP/CPP capacity, specialty volumes and a Rs 7 crore EBITDA rise at the specialty chemical subsidiary. PAT growth was moderate due to higher depreciation and interest, a Rs 7.2 crore exceptional provision at a Netherlands subsidiary and a Rs 5.3 crore deferred tax asset reversal in South Korea. For FY26, revenue rose 26% and EBITDA rose 32% to Rs 479 crore. Management said the capex cycle is largely complete, net debt fell Rs 75 crore over six months to Rs 1,159 crore, and it expects double-digit topline growth in FY27.

segments.name: BOPP/BOPET films
segments.commentary: BOPP margin about Rs 20/kg in Q4 vs Rs 13/kg in Dec-25 quarter; BOPET about Rs 18/kg vs Rs 12/kg in Dec-25 quarter. Films are about 90% BOPP-CPP and about 10% BOPET; specialty films are about 60% of films in Q4 (56-57% for full year).

segments.name: Specialty chemicals (subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 sales Rs 54 crore with 25%+ EBITDA; FY26 sales Rs 204 crore. Value growth was about 10% because raw-material-linked pricing was lower, though volume grew about 20%.

segments.name: Cosmo Plastech (rigid packaging)
segments.commentary: Q4 topline up over 70% YoY; reached EBITDA breakeven in Q4 with a small PBT loss likely. FY26 turnover about Rs 92 crore. Management targets high single-digit EBITDA in FY27 and mid-to-high teens in FY28.

segments.name: Zigly (petcare)
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 topline up 54% YoY; annualised run rate about Rs 90 crore. Plan to move it into a separate subsidiary in FY27, with possible external capital.

segments.name: Cosmo Consumer (window films, PPF, ceramic coatings)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue Rs 23 crore; exit annualised run rate about Rs 38 crore. Gross margin expected at 35-40%; still loss-making due to brand marketing. Management says at least two years to profitability and targets Rs 100 crore revenue first.

guidance_outlook: FY27 topline to grow in double digits, driven by utilisation of BOPP/CPP capacity added in FY26 and new businesses.
No EBITDA guidance given; management cited industry-cycle uncertainty but expects decent margins from new businesses, specialty growth and the US subsidiary.
Film volume growth potential of 15-20% from existing capacity; chemicals potential about Rs 100 crore more revenue; Plastech potential 30%; Cosmo Consumer at about 20% utilisation.
Capex for FY27 expected below Rs 100 crore; investment in Plastech, Consumer and Zigly about Rs 50-75 crore over next year and the year after.
Net debt to fall further; target to bring debt below 2x EBITDA within 12-18 months (currently 2.4x).
US tariff refund of more than Rs 60 crore expected over 6-12 months, partly payable back to customers; flows to both P&L and cash flow. Management expects Q1 FY27 to be better than Q4 FY26.
Operating cost (employee and other) expected to hold at Q4 run-rate plus inflation in FY27.
Dividend of Rs 4 per share recommended for FY26, subject to shareholder approval.

Cosmo Consumer and Plastech still loss-making at PBT level; Cosmo Consumer will keep losing money in FY27 as marketing continues.
Net debt of Rs 1,159 crore (2.4x EBITDA) and potential interest-rate pressure from inflation; deleveraging target below 2x within 12-18 months.
Timing and size of US tariff refund (above Rs 60 crore, partly payable to customers) remains uncertain.
Management gave no quantitative EBITDA guidance and called the outlook highly uncertain.

Indiannica (CBSE subsidiary) posted INR42 crore sales and a INR16 crore loss, and is to be merged into Navneet.

508989|2026-09.headline: Navneet Q2 FY27 standalone revenue rose about 31% to INR324 crore and standalone EBITDA rose 150% to INR20 crore, with margin at 6.2%.

Standalone PAT was INR6 crore versus a loss of INR6 crore a year earlier. Publication revenue rose about 53.8% to INR140 crore, partly on Q1 spillover, while domestic and export stationery margins were pressured by brand spending, manpower, a GST reversal, new plant depreciation and export discounts given under US tariffs. Management guided to better H2 profitability and said the K12 Techno stake sale proceeds (INR330 crore received, up to INR70 crore more pending) are to be deployed after a board decision.

509079|2026-03.headline: Gufic Q4 FY26 revenue rose about 23% YoY to INR252 crore with EBITDA margin at 17.7%, while FY26 PAT fell to INR63.2 crore.
509079|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 was the strongest quarter in company history, with revenue of about INR252 crore (vs INR205 crore in Q4 FY25), EBITDA of INR44.7 crore (17.73% margin vs 13.17%) and PAT of INR20.5 crore (vs INR8 crore). Full-year revenue rose to INR940.5 crore (from INR820 crore), but EBITDA margin eased to 16.26% and PAT fell to INR63.2 crore from INR69.9 crore, reflecting Indore fixed costs, a domestic critical-care working-capital reset worth about INR22 crore of revenue, and higher overheads. Indore reached EBITDA breakeven in Q4 at about 30% capacity utilisation, as committed. Management guided to about 15% revenue growth in FY27, around 18% EBITDA margin for FY27, and gross debt held at about INR400 crore.

segments.name: Indore (CMO / complex injectables)
segments.commentary: Reached 30% capacity utilisation by year-end as targeted and EBITDA breakeven in Q4. 40 tech transfers complete, 27 under development; 200-plus state FDA approvals; more than 20 Indian pharma companies use it as CMO base. Management expects Indore margin of about 31-32% at full utilisation, with overall Indore margin around 20%.

segments.name: Navsari (existing plant)
segments.commentary: Management said Navsari margin was about 20% and expects it to settle at 18-18.5% as costs rise. Navsari is building cartridge and pen GLP-1 capabilities.

segments.name: Domestic / Critical Care
segments.commentary: About 48-50% of revenue. 509079|2026-09.headline: Gufic Q2 FY27 revenue rose 25% YoY to INR288.4 crore, with EBITDA margin up to 17.23% despite API and freight cost pressure.
509079|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations was INR288.4 crore versus INR230.4 crore a year earlier, and EBITDA rose to INR49.7 crore from INR37.9 crore. Half-year revenue reached INR549.2 crore (INR457.3 crore prior year) with PAT of INR46 crore (INR27 crore). Management attributed the sequential margin dip to rupee-driven API import costs and higher domestic and international freight, and guided Q4 margin normalisation. Indore received three non-critical Form 483 observations after a US FDA pre-approval inspection, with EU compliance report submitted and UK clearance reported on the call. Working capital and borrowings rose on higher inventory held against the US/Iran conflict and US validation batches.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guided the gross margin dip to normalise by Q4 FY27 and FY28 EBITDA margin around 18.5% (H1 FY27 at 17.64%), rising toward 22-25% at least 1% a year; Indore EBITDA breakeven was reached in Q2 and is expected to cover interest and depreciation by Q4 FY27.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Indore four-line output is up QoQ and depot suite is ready for trials, but no new plant or line is committed; EU site addition is hoped for by September 2027 and US supply by Q2-Q3 2028, both dependent on regulators and client ANDA timelines.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Hospital injectable volumes grew 30-35% and international grew 20-22% in H1; international registrations (Saudi Arabia, Chile, UK, Germany, Italy, five more European countries) and semaglutide in 22 countries back continued growth, though domestic is guided at only 12-15%.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex is held at INR20-30 crore per year (about INR22-25 crore this year) funded from internal accruals and mainly maintenance-type; no utilisation figure was given and no large new project was announced.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management reiterated 15-20% FY27 revenue growth (domestic 12-15%) and gave no sign of a raise; hospital injectables face price erosion (meropenem from INR50,000 to INR33,000 per kg) that caps value growth at 8-10% on 30-35% volume growth.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q3 margin may still be pressured by rupee-driven API costs and freight, Indore US/EU certification timing is outside management control, and US supply depends on client ANDA timelines; the 17.23% margin already fell from 18.1%.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Four to six further molecules to be qualified at Indore between Nov 2026 and Mar 2027; dermal fillers expected around January; semaglutide revenue to ramp from Q1-Q2 next year; spray-dried lipid antifungal near completion.

rows.label: Inventory reduction to INR325-330 crore
rows.why: Inventory is about INR370 crore, with INR40-50 crore held as extra buffer against US-Iran supply risk; management expects INR325-330 crore by March 2027 but was cautious on normalisation.

rows.label: EU site addition and US market entry
rows.why: EU entry hoped for by September 2027 after a smoke-study delay of about 45 days; US supply hoped for Q2-Q3 2028 and tied to client ANDA goal dates, with EUR 1.5-1.6 million registration spend to finish by March 2027 and 182 MAs targeted by December 2027.

rows.label: Hospital injectable price erosion
rows.why: Meropenem fell from INR50,000 to INR33,000 per kg, and cephalosporin and piperacillin prices eased from October, though meropenem and hormone prices remain high; value growth is only 8-10% against 30-35% volume growth.

tone.note: Management was confident on Indore's regulatory progress and margin direction, but cautious on US supply timing and working-capital normalisation; analysts pressed on the gross margin dip, rising debt and working capital, and peak revenue potential, which management declined to forecast directly.
